reviews.creator: Trypadel
reviews.quote: Elle ne t'aide pas, mais elle amplifie ce que tu fais.
reviews.summary: Tests the Bullpadel Vertex 05 2026 and notes the slightly bouncy response from the 12K carbon layers. Finds the ball must be hit in the centre of the racket, because off-centre hits do not come out well. Calls it not the most forgiving, but pleasant in the hand, with the Vertex DNA coming through. Rates it as a real weapon on overhead shots, powerful but not easy power, and says the ball leaves once the player commits. Concludes it rewards active players, does not help them, and amplifies what they do, which makes it formidable for those who play forward.
highlights: formidable for those who play forward

reviews.creator: Llames13_
reviews.quote: es la pala más polivalente que he encontrado en toda la línea de Bullpadel
reviews.summary: Calls it the favorite of the whole 2026 Bullpadel line and the most versatile racket found in the range. Describes a medium feel that is fairly comfortable, fairly controllable and very manoeuvrable in every situation. Notes a slightly dry touch that adds a sense of control without being annoying or exaggerated. Feels it has gained some control compared with earlier years while losing practically no power. Plans to use it as their racket for 2026, after trying it on loan from a shop.
highlights: most versatile racket found in the range

reviews.trade: Slightly dry touch, though not annoying.

reviews.creator: Racketlife
reviews.quote: Det her bat er en sand klassiker
reviews.summary: Notes that the 2026 edition brings a new bridge and a rough surface on top that feels slightly grittier than in earlier years. Finds the racket very light in hand, listed at 365 to 375 grams, and lighter still subjectively. Describes a crisp, solid hit that still shoots the ball out of the racket in a lively way. Says this helps create power, so it suits players who struggle to generate pace themselves. Finds it easy to carry in defence for a power racket, since the listed high balance does not feel that high. Suggests adding 5 grams around the top for a bit more head-heavy balance. Calls it a true classic.

reviews.creator: Padel Review
reviews.quote: Non un cannone, ma se spingi la palla esce.
reviews.summary: Tests the new Vertex 05 on court with a playing partner, weighing it at 368 g with a balance of 25.1. Calls it a polyvalent diamond racket for intermediate to advanced players, more men than women. Finds the sweet spot not huge but not small, with a lower balance from the new bridge and slightly more ball exit than last year. Rates control as very good and handling easy, but power is limited: not a cannon, it gives what the player puts in. Finds spin good but a little less than last year. Calls the price very high. Scores most categories around 7.
reviews.more: Notes the new bridge lowers the balance and the surface is less sanded than last year's model. Finds it less bulky than earlier Vertex rackets, with a head that feels smaller. Finds the ball exit quick but controlled at the net and the racket solid, though a little lacking in aggression. Says the weight needs good timing on some shots. Calls the price of a top Bullpadel a lot for this model.
highlights: the sweet spot not huge but not small

reviews.stood: Good control and easy handling thanks to the lower balance from the new bridge.
reviews.trade: Limited raw power and a high price.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.quote: la sensación de control de esta verte 05 es muy buena
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Vertex 05 on court in baseline play, net play and overhead shots, with a unit weighing 366 g and a balance of 252 mm. Finds the control much improved, calling it a racket that now belongs in the control category. Rates the sweet spot as wide and the maneuverability as better than last year thanks to the lower balance. Notes the medium dry feel and sandy rough surface give good ball output and grip, though swings need to be lengthened at low speeds. Finds power only adequate, with flat volleys and hard smashes losing some bite. Suits players who prepare points and want safety.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 model, noting the same diamond shape but a slightly thicker core at the bottom, which they believe affects the balance. Points out the cord now exits from the centre of the cap and the grip is standard size. Wonders how the sandy rough finish will age. Finds the rough surface gives good spin on the volley without the ball rising. Advises finishing the rolling smash downward so the ball does not float.
highlights: Rates the sweet spot as wide

reviews.creator: Setup Padel | Mario Pazos
reviews.quote: es una pala que te va a ayudar muchísimo a subir de nivel
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Vertex 05 by judging ball output, hardness, sweet spot, control and power one by one rather than on court shots. Finds a good ball output that makes it forgiving from the back of the court. Rates the hardness as medium to medium low, the lowest hardness step in the Proline range. Calls the sweet spot standard plus and forgiving on late balls. Finds good handling thanks to the Air Power opening. Says power is where it gives something up, the least powerful in the range, and smashes get harder away from the net. Recommends it to players moving from beginner to intermediate, though they would not choose it for their own attacking game.
reviews.more: Notes the new Vertex Core takes some weight from the middle of the racket, a change that would not make them buy it. Likes that the cord now exits from the centre of the cap. Says the removable dampers add stiffness, and taking them out widens the sweet spot and lowers the weight. Finds the white finish attractive but easy to stain, and the sandy rough wears faster than a 3D rough.

reviews.keyPoint: Most versatile Proline racket, but the least powerful.
reviews.stood: Versatile all-round racket with good ball output and a forgiving sweet spot.
reviews.trade: Least powerful in the Proline range, harder to smash from far from the net.

reviews.creator: Otro Nivel Padel
reviews.quote: I think this is overall a fantastic racket, but it's not for everybody
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Vertex line side by side on court, including the normal Vertex 05. Finds it the most powerful Bullpadel racket when the ball is hit high on the face, with a smash that flies. Rates the sweet spot as medium, neither small nor big, and notes it has no dead spots when a hit is off. Calls the stiffness the only negative, though some players like a stiff racket. Calls it a fantastic racket but not for everybody, only for pro level male players with good timing. Gives it 8.7 out of 10, up from 8.2 after playing outdoors.
reviews.more: Compares it with the rest of the line. Finds the Vertex Geo easier to use than the normal Vertex, sitting between it and the Vertex Hybrid. Calls the Hybrid the best hybrid option, with a bigger sweet spot than the Geo. Rates the Women version as the softest and easiest to use, though possibly too soft for some men. Ranks the normal Vertex first for pure power.
highlights: Rates the sweet spot as medium
Calls the stiffness the only negative
pro level male players with good timing

reviews.quote: pero es una pala muy completa
reviews.summary: Describes the 2026 Vertex 05 as a diamond shape without a high balance, with a dry medium feel and a sweet spot in the medium high zone that is not hard to find. Finds it versatile, losing nothing in power or control, though other rackets are more powerful or more manageable. Notes the reinforced heart area, a slightly lower balance this year and no string coming out at the side, and measures 25.8 after swapping a part for the new dampeners, which raised it a little. Says it suits players who dislike a high balance diamond or a round low balance racket. Expects the price to drop in a few months.

sweet spot in the medium high zone

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: Siempre hemos dicho que la Vertex es una pala super polivalente
reviews.summary: Compares the 2026 Vertex 05 with the Vertex 05 Geo court zone by court zone. Measures their unit at 25.8 cm balance and 370 g, with a reinforced heart area, 12K carbon and MultiEva rubber. Finds it more manageable than the Geo despite the extra weight, with a medium hardness, a dry feel and a slightly bigger sweet spot. Likes the sandy rough finish at the net, though volleys lack some bite when pressing. Rates it level with the Geo at the net and on the bandeja, and behind it on smash. Calls it a very versatile racket that keeps its classic dry control.
reviews.more: Finds the 2026 unit smashes better than last year's, but credits the extra weight, 370 g against 357 g, more than any design change. Says the Vertex is better from the back of the court, while the Geo is slightly harder, more reactive and stronger on power. Notes the heart was thickened, possibly because players reported cracks. Suggests the Vertex for medium hardness with a dry feel that helps control fast balls, and the Geo for a touch more attack.

reviews.trade: Volleys lack some bite when pressing, and smash power trails the Geo.

reviews.creator: PadelLab
reviews.quote: se controla muy bien en toda la cancha
reviews.summary: Compares the 2026 Vertex 05 with the Geo version, covering shape, setup and feel. Puts the balance at about 25.1 to 25.2 cm and the weight at 365 to 375 g, with 12K carbon faces. Finds a medium balance hybrid that controls well all over the court and still has good power. Likes the strap now coming out of the middle of the cap and the included shockouts, which let players raise or lower the balance. Puts the feel near an AT10 18K, with a little more hardness. Recommends it to any level wanting a complete racket, not to players seeking extreme power or control.
reviews.more: Describes the Geo as similar but with more power, thanks to a higher balance of about 25.3 to 25.4 cm and a harder 3K face. Finds it sends the ball out faster on smashes and viboras and helps at the net, but asks for more push and a longer finish from the back. Suggests it for players moving up from a hybrid or control racket who want extra power.

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: Se ci metti gambe, se ci metti braccio, funziona.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Vertex 05 on court after weighing it at 369 g with a declared balance of 26 cm. Finds it a classic, complete diamond with a medium sweet spot that is better than expected and a progressive, controllable feel. Likes it most at the net, scoring volleys 8.5 out of 10, and finds ball exit generous at medium pace. Notes a slightly dry touch, so players with sensitive arms should avoid it. Calls it more controllable and spinnier than the Vertex 05 Geo but less explosive on overheads. Says it suits full intermediate to advanced players, and finds the price too high.
reviews.more: Prefers it to the Vertex 05 Geo overall for control, spin and predictability, though likes the Geo feel more. Places it between Metalbone Soft and Metalbone Hard, closest to the HRD+, with a lower balance. Sees similarities with the Combat Etna, which is stiffer, and finds the Extreme Pro has a livelier touch but less spin. Recommends fitting an aftermarket grip in place of the stock grip, which weighs about 6 to 8 g more than grips from other brands. Notes the strap exit is now central.

players with sensitive arms should avoid it

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: Trovo eccellente il taglio di questa Vertex 05.
reviews.summary: Tests the diamond shaped racket on court with a score out of ten for each shot, giving nine for high balls, basic shots, high wall exits, blocks and smash. Finds the slice excellent and the low balance easy on the arm, with a sweet spot running from the logo down to the centre. Notes that the multi EVA core gives comfort but not maximum power, and measures impact around 6.5 with slightly high vibrations that the factory shockout dampens. Rates the price poorly, though shops already sell it for less. Suits intermediate advanced to semi-pro players.
reviews.more: Says the Vertex 05 Geo pleased very much on blocks too, and this one also earns a nine there. Finds the newer Bullpadel rackets more reliable than those of the last two or three years. Calls the lob excellent even when hit from a decentred position. Dislikes that dampening parts are needed from the factory. Says it is powerful, just not a cannon, and fits semi-competitive players such as Serie D or team cup players rather than top competitors.

sweet spot running from the logo
price a four out of ten

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: C'est bien plus puissant que la version précédente.
reviews.summary: Compares the 2026 diamond shape with 12K carbon against the Geo version, measuring 370 g and a balance of 263 mm, much higher than the 251 mm of the 2025 model. Finds it very reactive, with good ball speed and length, and clearly more powerful than the previous version in smashes. Calls it made for aggressive players who finish points. Notes it is much less tolerant, forgiving little when the ball is hit off centre. Rates handling as correct, though below the 2025 model. Recommends it for left-side attackers with a good technical base, level 5 and above, who want to maximise power.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Geo, which uses 3K carbon, a more angular shape and a lower 258 mm balance at the same 370 g. Finds the Geo more comfortable, more stable and easier in defence, with better control on high shots, but much weaker in smashes. Would keep the Geo over the classic model, as it seems easier to play and less tiring in the long term. Advises trying both rackets before choosing.
highlights: clearly more powerful than the previous version
left-side attackers with a good technical base

reviews.stood: Reactive and clearly more powerful in smashes than the 2025 model.
reviews.trade: Much less tolerant, forgives little when the ball is hit off centre.

reviews.creator: Mejora Tu Padel
reviews.quote: Da la sensación de tener un punto dulce más amplio también
reviews.summary: Tests it against the Hack 04 in defence, attack, power and drop shot tests with a second player. Finds the core medium soft, with a wider sweet spot, more feel and more comfort in cold weather than the Hack. Calls it very manageable, though the grip is thick and short, and the ball can fly out on volleys if the hand opens. Notes the Gesacore grip, vibration damping and custom weight system. Sees the Hack giving more raw power, but the Vertex landing better hits more often. Recommends it to players who struggle in defence or play in cold conditions.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Hack 04, an 18K tricarbon racket with a medium hard core. Finds the Hack gives more raw power but misses timing more often, while the Vertex hits more effectively. Gives the Vertex the win for practicality. Suggests removing the Gesacore cover or fitting a normal grip if the hand is small. Likes the custom weight system that lets players add weight for more punch. Wants an interchangeable wrist strap.

reviews.keyPoint: Versatile power racket that stays manageable and comfortable.
reviews.stood: Wider sweet spot, softer feel and easy handling compared with the Hack 04.
reviews.trade: Thick short grip and less raw power than the Hack 04.

reviews.creator: The Padel School
reviews.quote: Nice firm contact on the ball actually for an all round racket.
reviews.summary: Tests the Vertex 05 against the Geo version, describing the 12K carbon face as firmer with a balance not as high, aimed at a more all round player. Finds nice firm contact and good feel, with power that feels accurate rather than uncontrollable. Gets similar control at the back of the court and can maneuver the ball well, but gets less power than from the Geo, especially on overheads and aggressive volleys. Calls it quite forgiving and says control was available on all shots. Rates it an excellent all round racket and recommends it from intermediate level and up.
reviews.more: Notes changes from last season: curve active technology, different custom weighting in the top, a larger surface area that adds forgiveness, and the Vertex core, which adds stability. Points out that both versions share Ease Vibe technology and the Hessa grip, which reduce vibration and arm strain. Describes the Geo as having more surface area, 3K carbon, a larger sweet spot, more rebound and a more offensive feel, with a bit more power overall.

less power than from the Geo
recommends it from intermediate level and up

Finds slightly more ball output, still medium to medium low, with a dry feel that asks players to accompany and extend shots. Feels more comfortable in defence than the 2025. Finds the sandy rough texture less marked on their unit. Calls it versatile, with good control.

reviews.creator: EverythingPadel
reviews.quote: Some of my best performances this year have been with this racket.
reviews.summary: Uses it for many months after first trying the 12K for about a month and a half. Finds the 18K slightly softer than the 12K and prefers it even more, possibly helped by the black design. Rates the balance of power and control as really good in a teardrop shape, with enough spin for the left or right side. Calls the maneuverability great and the feel really comfortable in the hand. Finds the sweet spot very big. Thinks it suits right side players a little more because the softer face is slightly more control based. Credits it with some of their best performances this year.
reviews.more: Describes the 12K as having unbelievable control and being forgiving in defence on the right side, with a big sweet spot, but chose the 18K for its softer feel. Notes that their own signature racket is slightly lighter than the 18K and 12K, which makes it more maneuverable in volley battles and defence at a slight cost to power. Says the 18K can be used on either side.

reviews.trade: Slightly more control based, so it suits right side players a little more.

reviews.creator: Tino
reviews.quote: Powernya emang lebih kerasa, cuma untuk kontrolnya buat gua jauh lebih sulit
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 18K after already playing the 2024 and 2025 versions, and finds it suits left-side, attacking players rather than a right-side control player. Feels the foam is firmer and harder than the 2025 18K, so the change felt strange and power is more noticeable but control is much harder. Likes the look, the grip feel and the combined 3D honeycomb and sand surface. Weighs it at 374 g with grip against a listed 370 g. Plans to sell it after two sessions, saying it is a good racket that does not match a defensive control style.
reviews.more: Rates the 2025 18K as the best for a control-minded right-side player, above both 2024 and 2026. Hears that the 2026 18K feels closer to the 2025 12K, so the lineup looks swapped this year. Notes the included weights: black ones add 2 g per side and red ones 4 g per side, though they have not used them yet. Admits it may need around five sessions to adapt. Considered the Bullpadel Vertex 05 but disliked its blue colour. Advises checking build quality and registering the barcode to avoid fakes.

reviews.stood: Looks luxurious and the grip feels good, with more noticeable power.
reviews.trade: Control is much harder for a right-side defensive player.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2025, Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2024, Bullpadel Vertex 05

reviews.creator: Padel Elite Barletta
reviews.quote: Il punto dolce risulta essere un po' più ampio della 12K.
reviews.summary: Compares the 18K with the new 12K Extreme after trying both. Finds the 18K close to the 2025 version, with a rougher surface and a slightly stiffer feel. Calls it the more controlled, precise and quick of the two, with good power. Notes a wider sweet spot than the 12K and more rubber feel at low rhythm, with easier ball output. Finds it gives less push than the 12K when attacking and feels less full. Rates both as versatile rackets for a wide audience, and says the choice depends on wanting speed and feel or a fuller, more aggressive racket.
reviews.more: Says Agustin Tapia alternates both rackets, using the 18K more early in the season and then the 12K almost always for extra push at high rhythm. Notes the two use different rubbers and that the carbon on the 12K Extreme is woven differently. Describes the 12K as a bit more aggressive and the 18K as the pick for more feel and speed.
highlights: less push than the 12K when attacking

reviews.trade: Gives less push than the 12K when attacking and feels less full.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 Genius 12K Extreme 2026, Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2025

reviews.creator: Super Padel Bros
reviews.quote: Il punto dolce è più ampio e migliore rispetto alla 12K
reviews.summary: Tests it without the head weights, after being disappointed by the 12K. Finds the touch drier and more honest, with a wider sweet spot and better control than the 12K, plus zero vibrations. Rates the baseline game 8.5, the volley 7, and the bandeja, vibora and smash 8 each. Notes that power and spin are lacking, so players need more arm on defence and high wall exits. Calls the ball exit weaker because of the MLD Black Eva rubber. Suggests adding head weights for power. Recommends it to advanced beginners up to advanced players, and says the 2025 18K gives similar performance for less.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 12K throughout: the 12K has a harder, more reactive HR3 Black Eva rubber and more power, but a confusing feel at impact. Finds the grip comfortable for a medium small hand, and the strap well made. Notes the surface is rough rather than sandblasted, which helps spin only a little. Points out that retail AT10 rackets are not the ones Tapia uses. Rates looks 8.5. Says the 2025 18K is the better buy, since two fit in the same budget.

reviews.stood: Sincere, communicative touch with a wide sweet spot and excellent comfort.
reviews.trade: Lacks power and spin, especially on volleys and high wall exits.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 Genius 12K, Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2025, OxDog Ultimate Pro 2025

reviews.creator: Padel Review
reviews.quote: è una racchetta che richiede tecnica e precisione
reviews.summary: Plays it on court and compares it with the 12K, finding it stiffer and more powerful at high swing speeds. Measures 364 g with a medium balance of 25.6 cm and calls it totally easy to move. Finds the sweet spot small, so imprecise contact sends balls too short or too long. Feels it unstable when hit hard from the back of the court without an overgrip. Rates spin as good and says lobs, vibora and cut shots work well. Notes it demands technique and precision at the net and overhead too. Calls the price excessive. Suits intermediate to advanced players on either side.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 12K, calling it stiffer, more offensive and giving more control and feel. Says the 12K has a slightly more trampoline effect, while this one lacks some inertia and is only powerful if the player brings the power. Recalls that the removable weights failed on the 12K, but thinks they might make more sense here. Calls it a technical racket that is not for everyone.
highlights: more powerful at high swing speeds

reviews.keyPoint: Stiff technical racket that rewards precise players only.
reviews.stood: Very easy to move, with good feel and spin.
reviews.trade: Small sweet spot and high price, punishes imprecise contact.

reviews.creator: padelwithmax
reviews.quote: this racket gave me a lot of control and precision
reviews.summary: Tests the hybrid shape with dual roughness against the 12K version and finds it slightly softer, with more feel and control from the back of the court. Notes a slightly bigger sweet spot and a little more maneuverability. Finds extra touch and precision at the net for drop volleys and angles, but less zip and power in volleys than the 12K. Gets a lot of control on placement, though with less pace. Produces enough power and spin on overheads, but the softer feel means the ball does not travel as far. Suits advanced players who build points with precision and control. Rates it 9.4 out of 10.
highlights: extra touch and precision at the net
less zip and power in volleys

reviews.trade: Less zip and pace in volleys and overheads than the 12K.

reviews.creator: InfoPalas
reviews.quote: es una pala extremadamente manejable
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Nox AT10 Genius 18K for a couple of days on loan, in a 362 g unit with a balance of about 250 mm. Finds it extremely manageable, moving almost like a feather, with a response that does not force the player to push the ball. Rates defence well but not outstanding, as it will not save extreme situations, and finds the control very good. Notes the sweet spot feels standard size, with some off centre hits at the net and on overheads. Finds the double rough texture effective. Suits players who want comfort and control in defence with acceptable attacking ability.
reviews.more: Finds the low balance can be raised with weight strips of 2 and 4 g on the top edge, though the test was done without them. Misses some inertia on longer swings and on smashes, where more acceleration is needed. Rates bandeja and rulo well, since the swing is quick to set up. Compares the control feel with Neuron style rackets that need more pushing, saying this one does not. Notes the Custom Grips and the Nox reputation for caring for the elbow.
highlights: the sweet spot feels standard size
Finds the double rough texture effective

reviews.stood: Extremely light feel in hand with good control and a correct ball exit.
reviews.trade: Less inertia on smashes and long swings, and only a standard sweet spot.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.quote: el punto dulce está muy bien optimizado
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 18K on court with the 4 g counterweights fitted, after trying the stock setup and the 2 g setup. Measures 363 g and 252 mm balance without weights, and 371 g with 259 mm using the 4 g pair. Finds the sweet spot very well optimised and the medium plus feel controllable at high speed, with the two density rubber giving decent ball exit at medium pace. Rates the new 3D sandy texture as good grip that adds spin. Calls it balanced at the net, though not very reactive, so it asks for arm acceleration on the viper. Suits players who want control with some ball exit.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 version, finding similar depth and ball exit but better grip from the new texture. Notes that without weights it feels very manoeuvrable, close to a control racket, while the 4 g pair brings a near medium balance. Says the weights help the tip drop on smashes and keep the ball from floating. Says the 2 g pair gives a more balanced feel with less noticeable weight. Expects decent durability but wants to see how the sandy finish ages.
highlights: asks for arm acceleration on the viper

reviews.stood: Well optimised sweet spot and a 3D texture that gives good grip.
reviews.trade: Not very reactive, so it needs arm acceleration, and weights cost some manoeuvrability.

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: È una racchetta facile, giocabile, apprezzabile per tante cose
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 AT10 18K at its stock weight, without adding the adhesive weights, to judge it fairly against other rackets. Finds an actual weight of 355 g against 368 g declared, and a low balance around 25 cm. Rates it easy, forgiving and good for spin, with a wider sweet spot than the 12K. Misses head weight and impact feel when playing fast, and finds control fades when hitting harder. Calls it an intermediate racket, best for intermediate to advanced intermediate players, and says the price is too high for the performance. Suggests the cheaper 2025 model instead.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 model, which feels close and costs about half, with the 2026 adding a single face finish, tunnel slots for adhesive weights and slightly better control. Prefers the AT10 Attack, which has several gears more. Names the Starvie Raptor and Adidas Metalbone Ctrl Carbon as alternatives, the latter at a lower street price. Notes the finishing looks poor for the price and the adhesive weights come off easily.

reviews.stood: Easy to play, good spin and a wide central sweet spot.
reviews.trade: Too expensive for its performance and short on head weight.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2025, Nox AT10 Genius 12K, Nox AT10 Genius Attack, Starvie Raptor, Adidas Metalbone Ctrl Carbon

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.quote: una pala un poquito para todo, siempre y cuando te guste esta dureza media
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 model on court by zone, with two overgrips and a weight of 364 g, balance 25.8 to 25.9 cm. Finds it very manoeuvrable, with a slightly larger centred sweet spot and good ball output at medium and medium low pace. Notes the light head makes the ball float when accelerating unless the tip is pulled down, and that power in the smash is a step below the AT10 12K Extreme. Likes the new rough surface and optional head weights over last year. Suits players wanting a versatile medium hardness racket, including those with elbow trouble, but sees the price gap as not worth the change.
reviews.more: Compares it with last year's model and finds the new full face rough texture lets the ball slip less, which helps when adding spin and weight on vibora and bandeja. Adds that fitting the 2 g or 4 g head weights, or a protector, helps pull the tip down for smashes and volleys, at some cost in handling. Places it next to the Bullpadel Vertex as a medium hardness reference, with more handling and a little more ball output.

a step below the AT10 12K Extreme

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: Una pala maneggevole con punto dolce ampio che non senti sul braccio
reviews.summary: Tests the racket on court and scores each shot out of 10, giving 10 for the high ball, 10 for the low wall exit and basic shots, and 9.5 for the high wall exit and the block. Finds the sweet spot very wide, helping on off-centre hits, with almost no vibration on the arm. Calls it handy and versatile, with a little more power on the smash than the 12K but not maximum power. Rates the price as too high for a racket made in Pakistan. Sees it suiting intermediate to competitive players.
reviews.more: Compares it with the white 12K, finding slightly more punch on the smash but less overall power, with a different rubber and carbon. Rates the impact type 6.6 against 6.5, a little harder and more closed, but not softer than the 12K. Notes that Nox raised the level this year compared with last year's blander rackets. Removes the stock grip because of personal taste. Mentions the Weight Balance system with 2 g black and 4 g red weights.
highlights: almost no vibration on the arm
a little more power on the smash

reviews.stood: Handy racket with a very wide sweet spot and almost no arm vibration.
reviews.trade: Not maximum power, and it is rated 4.5 out of 10 for value.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.summary: Finds it more comfortable and forgiving in defence than the 12K Alum Xtrem. Notes precise touch and good output on slow play and placed volleys. Finds lob height takes more physical effort, and aggressive volleys need precise timing. Finds overheads less controlled, and smash power trails the 12K.
highlights: more comfortable and forgiving in defence

reviews.keyPoint: Forgiving in defence but short on smash power.
reviews.stood: More comfortable and forgiving in defence, with precise touch.
reviews.trade: Lobs take more effort, overheads feel less controlled and smash power trails the 12K.

reviews.creator: Peter Consuegra
reviews.quote: creo que es un palón, la verdad
reviews.summary: Tests the new aluminised 18K version on court across defence, volleys and overhead play, after going through the features Nox lists. Finds it very comfortable and easy to move at low speed, with a softer feel than the 12K model and a fairly wide sweet spot. Feels more at ease blocking than accelerating, and notes the ball stays in the racket when trying to speed up. Finds the víbora leaves quickly and needs more control, while the rulo felt easier than with the 12K aluminised. Calls it a hybrid that leans toward control, suited to levels up to intermediate, but not to beginners.
reviews.more: Describes a teardrop shape with medium balance, a full carbon frame, a multi-layer MLD Black Eva core and a wedge system for adding weight. Explains that the core differs from last year's 18K, so the feel changes more than just the face fibres. Treats it as a top-range racket and a sizeable investment. Advises beginners to choose a cheaper model, but expects other players to be happy with it.
highlights: more at ease blocking than accelerating

reviews.trade: Harder to accelerate and to control the víbora; top-range price for beginners.

reviews.creator: el4Set
reviews.quote: Es como conseguir más con menos
reviews.summary: Tests all five 2026 AT10 rackets on court, covering defence, volleys, bandeja and vibora, plus a smash distance test. Finds the hybrid 18K more comfortable and less dry than the 12K, with a slightly wider sweet spot and more ball output for less effort. Notes that the ball sinks into the racket more than on the 12K, and that last year's 18K feels almost the same. Measures 358 g and a balance of 25.4 cm with their setup, stock grip removed and two overgrips added. Finds a lower performance ceiling and less control than the 12K. Calls it the easiest way to play aggressively and the option most players could like.
reviews.more: Compares it with the hybrid 12K, which feels drier, needs a firmer hit and gives more control but is more technical. Rates the 12K hybrid as the most complete of the range and prefers it for smashes, though differences in distance were very subtle. Notes the diamond 18K is easier than the 12K Attack but moves worse than the hybrid 18K, with a higher balance. Says all AT10 rackets share a sandy 3D rough surface that needs improving.
highlights: more ball output for less effort

reviews.stood: More comfortable feel and more ball output for less effort.
reviews.trade: Lower performance ceiling and less control than the 12K.

reviews.creator: Xeexi1707
reviews.quote: Es igual que la blanca, pero más blandita, más rebotona, diríamos.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 18K straight after the 12K, in defence, volleys, bandeja and smash. Finds it a touch softer than the 12K, with the ball sinking more into the face, which shows in the sound. Says it feels very close to the 2025 18K they play with. Rates it very manageable and comfortable, with good ball exit and little effort needed. Prefers the 12K in defence, cannot split them in attack, and leans slightly to the 18K for bandeja and smash. Calls it versatile rather than a power racket, suited to almost any player.
reviews.more: Notes the 2026 range adds a weight system for adjusting balance, new air channels for handling and a new double rough finish with 3D texture. Says last year's 18K had no rough texture in the X zone. Understands the Black EVA rubber is a little harder than last year. Picks the 12K overall, finding it a bit more comfortable, and says the two are otherwise the same racket apart from rubber and carbon.
highlights: versatile rather than a power racket

reviews.creator: Khaled Reda Alsayed Abd El Aaty
reviews.summary: Plays the Wilson Endure Pro V1 2026 for about three months before reviewing it, choosing to cover a racket few players have tried. Notes it is a Momo Gonzalez racket and the player's first Wilson sponsorship, with a hard core. Finds the weight distributed low and a bit annoying after three months of use. Calls the grip length medium and the strap only average for comfort. Describes the surface texture as rough and unusual, with a strange, dead sound. Does not feel it gives much spin. Adds match highlights at the end.

reviews.creator: Padel Ibérico — court test
reviews.quote: Pala superligera con un punto dulce gigante.
reviews.summary: Tests a round-shaped racket expecting a defensive feel and finds an aggressive one instead. Notes the balance is low, with a weight of 365 g in 3K, but says the protector raises the balance slightly and the 3K is not fully soft. Compares the feel to a diamond shape with a little more control and a hard response. Rates the rough surface Good, nothing extreme. Finds the rubber very reactive at high speed, so the ball leaves fast, and warns to be careful when lobbing. Calls it super light with a giant sweet spot. Recommends it to players who want to dominate the air and defend without a very high balance.

reviews.creator: Trypadel — court test
reviews.quote: C'est une raquette super rassurante.
reviews.summary: Tests the new Wilson Endure Pro V1 and calls it a very reassuring racket, likening it to playing with life insurance. Describes it as stable, precise and controlled, easy to use, with a large sweet spot. Finds lobs come out very clean and says a player could defend for hours without anything going wrong. Rates it as a 100 percent control racket where power is not the strong point, so hitting hard needs a full commitment to the swing. Finds placing vibora shots easy. Recommends it for players who value consistency, control and safety, and for building the point and keeping control in important moments.

reviews.creator: Justpadel — Sven Boele
reviews.quote: I cannot recommend this enough.
reviews.summary: Tests it on a slower court in the Netherlands in December with little sand. Finds the sweet spot bigger than on earlier Wilson rackets. Calls it one of the best rackets for slicing at the net, saying the amount of slice is immense for a round racket. Likes the kick smash, noting the thinner sides, and advises holding it relaxed and lower to get kick. Calls the smash very decent for a round racket. Rates it 9.5 out of 10 for pro level players and good intermediate players coming from tennis. Says it suits using wrist and hand for spin from the back.
reviews.more: Thinks Wilson is improving fast and did a very good job on the Endure line. Notes it is the racket Momo Gonzalez is going to play with. Says most players hold the racket too tight for the smash, which limits how far it goes. Describes the motion at the net as feeling fantastic and says it works well for players who want to play with spin from the back using wrist and hand.
reviews.short: Tests it on a slower court in the Netherlands in December with little sand. Finds the sweet spot bigger than on earlier Wilson rackets. Calls it one of the best rackets for slicing at the net, saying the amount of slice is immense for a round racket. Likes the kick smash, noting the thinner sides, and advises holding it relaxed and lower to get kick. Calls the smash very decent for a round racket. Rates it 9.5 out of 10 for pro level players and good intermediate players coming from tennis. Says it suits using wrist and hand for spin from the back.
reviews.keyPoint: Round racket that excels at net slice and kick smashes.
reviews.stood: Huge amount of slice at the net and plenty of kick on smashes.
reviews.trade: Smash needs a relaxed, lower grip to get distance.

reviews.creator: OngoalSweden — shared court test
reviews.summary: Finds the Pro slightly stiffer and less immediately responsive than the standard model. Finds fuller swings get better output from it. Notes the two rackets had different grip builds, including two wraps and a Noene anti-vibration layer.
highlights: slightly stiffer and less immediately responsive
reviews.short: Finds the Pro slightly stiffer and less immediately responsive than the standard model. Finds fuller swings get better output from it. Notes the two rackets had different grip builds, including two wraps and a Noene anti-vibration layer.
reviews.keyPoint: Slightly stiffer feel that rewards fuller swings.
reviews.stood: Better output on fuller swings.
reviews.trade: Slightly stiffer and less immediately responsive than the standard model.

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: Y la Pro para mí es la que más difícil es sacarle potencia
reviews.summary: Tests the Pro against the Endure and Endure LS on court, with a unit weighing 371 g and a 13 cm handle. Finds a very dry feel that gives good control of ball speed, with a sweet spot smaller than the standard Endure. Notes that hits above the centre of the face die, and that backhand volleys demand centred contact. Calls it the hardest of the three to get power from, especially on smashes, and the one needing the most technique. Rates handling slightly worse than the standard Endure. Suits technically strong players who want precise speed control.
reviews.more: Picks the standard Endure as the favourite of the three, for a bigger sweet spot and a better balance between dryness and reactivity. Finds the LS softer, more forgiving and better on smashes than expected. Notes all three share Control Foam, with 3K carbon faces on the Pro, and a string that cannot be swapped. Says the Pro struggles most on smashes and bandejas when hit high on the face, and would avoid bringing the ball back with any of them in a match. Reminds that control here means speed control, not a soft feel.
highlights: sweet spot smaller than the standard Endure
hardest of the three to get power from

reviews.keyPoint: Precise dry feel, but hard to generate power.
reviews.stood: Very precise control of ball speed when hit in the centre.
reviews.trade: Hard to extract power, punishes off-centre hits and needs good technique.

reviews.creator: Dani13
reviews.quote: me ha hecho sentirme bastante cómodo, con mucha confianza
reviews.summary: Tests the racket in four zones of the court: defence, vibora and bandeja, volleys and smashes. Finds a dry feel, medium-hard stiffness close to a Combat Fuji, and a very good sense of control. Measures 367 g with two overgrips and no original grip, and a balance of 26 cm. Rates handling as a strong point, never feeling physical in play. Notes the centred sweet spot: off-centre hits feel stiffer and come out shorter. Finds it more reactive when force is applied than at slow rhythms. Names volleys as the best zone and overhead play as the hardest to adapt to, mainly for players coming from other shapes.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Combat Fuji, Hack Hybrid and last year's Nox AT10 12K as direct rivals. Finds power easier to get from a Bela Pro or Defy Pro. Notes the rough 3K carbon is less sandy than a Siux ST4 Pro but should last longer. Advises pulling the tip down on vibora and bandeja so the ball does not fly straight. Calls the grip thinner than on the Bela and 13 cm long.
highlights: a very good sense of control
more reactive when force is applied

reviews.keyPoint: Dry, controlled and easy to handle if hit centrally.

reviews.compared: Combat Fuji, Hack Hybrid, Nox AT10 12K, Wilson Bela Pro, Wilson Defy Pro, Siux ST4 Pro

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: Ottimo controllo, ma poca uscita di palla.
reviews.summary: Tests it over three matches of good level and intensity, on both the right and left side. Finds the round head gives very good control, a medium-hard feel and a short adaptation period, with vibrations well handled and no arm fatigue. Notes that the ball needs some help to lift, so it can land short, and that it is not a smash cannon. Rates the rough surface as very good for spin and the handling as interesting for its weight. Sees it suiting intermediate to advanced players, not those who want brute power. Calls the price slightly high but worth it.
reviews.more: Compares the look with the Bela, finding it less striking but pleasant. Says the longer handle than usual Wilson allows two hands, helped by the knurling, which suits former tennis players. Notes the wrist cord does not exit from the centre but is less annoying than on a Bullpadel. Mentions the racket comes with a protector that adds a few grams. Points out the house weight range is 365 g plus or minus 10, and that around 360 to 365 g it plays well. Sees slow starters as a good fit.
reviews.short: Tests it over three matches of good level and intensity, on both the right and left side. reviews.keyPoint: Round racket with great control but modest ball exit.
reviews.stood: Very good control, easy to understand, with good vibration damping and spin.
reviews.trade: Not powerful enough for heavy hitters, and the ball needs help to rise.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: it’s truly the one that offers the most precision
reviews.summary: Tests the Endure Pro in a lab alongside the Classic and Light and Soft versions, measuring a weight of 365g, a balance of 257mm and a stiffness of 62 RA shared across the range. Notes the round shape, the Y-shaped bridge, a 13 cm handle and a 3K carbon face over the densest Control Foam Plus in the range. Finds it very easy to defend with, with the best feel and most precision of the three. Warns that it needs the most physical effort. Recommends it for intermediate players at level 5 to 6 with a good technical level and good physical fitness.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Classic, which has a balance of 255mm, unidirectional carbon and a drier feel with a less dense foam. Describes the Light and Soft version as lighter at 355g, with a balance of 260mm and a fiberglass face that gives the most comfort and forgiveness. Suggests the Classic for intermediate players at levels 4 to 6 and the Light and Soft for beginners or players looking to progress. Says the whole range is made for precision and touch.
highlights: densest Control Foam Plus in the range
reviews.short: Tests the Endure Pro in a lab alongside the Classic and Light and Soft versions, measuring a weight of 365g, a balance of 257mm and a stiffness of 62 RA shared across the range. reviews.keyPoint: Most precise racket in the range, but physically demanding.
reviews.stood: Best feel and most precision of the Endure range.
reviews.trade: Needs a good technical level and the most physical effort.
reviews.compared: Wilson Endure Classic, Wilson Endure Light and Soft

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: Non nasce come cannone, ma è un bel fucile
reviews.summary: Tests the Wilson Endure Pro V1 and finds it far from a purely defensive racket. Lists 3K carbon faces, 365 g, a balance of 26.2 cm in their sample, double density Control Foam Plus and an Exact Touch surface without relief that gives plenty of spin. Rates the impact feel as one of the best from Wilson, with control and good ball output from the back. Finds the sweet spot almost reassuring but central, since it is a round shape, and stiffer toward the tip. Calls volleys a surprise, with great touch. Notes real offensive potential, though less leverage than the sister models. Suits players wanting a complete, solid racket.
reviews.more: Points to the round shape as the reason the sweet spot stays central and does not suit very high impacts, where the sister models do better. Says handling is more than good, though the racket is heavier than expected. Finds good ball output on volleys and on shots from above. Describes it as not built as a cannon but a good rifle, with the double density rubber giving explosiveness.
highlights: far from a purely defensive racket
one of the best from Wilson

reviews.keyPoint: Complete round racket with more attacking output than expected.
reviews.stood: Excellent impact feel and touch, with spin and ball output on top.
reviews.trade: Round shape means a central sweet spot and a stiffer feel toward the tip.

reviews.creator: the4Set — Pablo
reviews.quote: It's a pretty firm racket that also performs well at high speeds
reviews.summary: Compares the 2026 Endure Pro with the Bela and the Defy Pro using a hardness test, ball output checks and play on court in Madrid. Notes it is the lightest at 365 g, with a 25.5 cm balance, a round shape and a semi hard feel. Finds the roughness unusual, neither sandy nor 3D, though it will last much longer than a sandy finish. Rates it the most precise and easiest to move of the three, with the least ball output. Finds less spin and speed on volleys, and more push needed in defense. Still prefers the Bela's roughness.
reviews.more: Ranks the Endure Pro against the Defy Pro and the Bela by situation. Gives the Endure Pro a technical tie with the Bela in defense, where it moves better but needs more push. Finds the Defy Pro the most aggressive on volleys and the farthest hitting in average distance tests, with the Endure Pro and Bela roughly level. Says hitting hard with the Endure Pro is still possible, though the low balance may not give an extra boost. Suggests it for players who want a round shape and control above all.
highlights: most precise and easiest to move

reviews.keyPoint: Round, light control racket with the least ball output.
reviews.stood: Most precise and easiest to move of the three Wilson rackets.
reviews.trade: Less spin and speed on volleys, and maybe no extra boost from the low balance.
reviews.compared: Wilson Bela V3, Wilson Defy Pro

reviews.creator: BizPadel — Alan Briñol
reviews.quote: I feel like it has the right control and right power.
reviews.summary: Looks for good balance and manageability, and finds the racket quick to move. Feels in control of where the ball goes, both from the back of the court and at the volley. Says it can slow the ball down or speed it up when under pressure, and gives the right depth without worry. Finds it helps in defence and in attack, with the right control and power. Calls the output really good, with the ball coming off the face nicely. Picks it for its nice touch and manageability, and says it moves very fast in the hand.
highlights: helps in defence and in attack

reviews.keyPoint: Controlled, easy to move racket with balanced power.
reviews.stood: Easy to move, with good control and a nice touch on the ball.

reviews.creator: Padel Review — Emiliano and Alvin
reviews.quote: una tonda con carattere
reviews.summary: Tests the round Wilson Endure Pro from the back of the court, at the net and overhead, with a tested weight of 373 g against a stated base of 365 g. Finds good control, a good sweet spot and a good feel on blocks and soft drop shots, but little ball exit, so lobs come up short without a firm swing. Feels the weight on the arm, especially on the backhand, though the longer handle helps with the second hand. Rates spin, flat smash and vibora well. Calls it a round racket with character that suits intermediate advanced players and up, with a trained arm, not an easy one.
reviews.more: Notes the price is in line with other top rackets. Describes 3K carbon faces, a new bridge and grip dots meant to help the non-dominant hand. Mentions the label calls it a racket for defensive players, while they find it needs a trained arm and a decisive impact. Says it can suit players on the left or the right side. Reports some vibration, but no elbow trouble.
highlights: longer handle helps with the second hand
reviews.short: Tests the round Wilson Endure Pro from the back of the court, at the net and overhead, with a tested weight of 373 g against a stated base of 365 g. reviews.keyPoint: Round racket with character that demands a trained arm.
reviews.stood: Good control, a solid feel on blocks and a helpful longer handle.
reviews.trade: Heavy and not very maneuverable, with little ball exit and some arm strain.

reviews.creator: Mejora Tu Padel — Manu Martín
reviews.quote: Yo he notado que la Endure Pro más inercia.
reviews.summary: Compares the three 2026 Endure models on court with a professional player, using rebounders and target drills from the back and at the net. Finds the Pro heavier and fuller than the LS, with more power and a straighter ball on groundstrokes and volleys. Notes a balance of 260 mm and 365 g, a harder 3K carbon face and a drier feel aimed at high intensity players. Accelerates worse on overhead shots, but finds inertia helps when missing the sweet spot. Picks it over the standard version for personal use.
reviews.more: Finds the standard Endure easier to accelerate and more manageable for drop shots, with a slightly softer feel, while the Pro needs more effort to move. Hears the professional player choose the standard version as the better fit for a defensive player who also likes to attack. Calls the Pro a better match for players who attack more and want a firm feel.
highlights: straighter ball on groundstrokes and volleys
inertia helps when missing the sweet spot

reviews.keyPoint: Heavier and straighter, but slower to accelerate overhead.
reviews.stood: More inertia, so the ball goes straighter from the back and at the net.
reviews.trade: Accelerates worse overhead and takes more effort to move than the lighter versions.
reviews.compared: Wilson Endure V1, Wilson Endure LS

reviews.creator: Padel Test — Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: la pala rotonda più potente che io abbia mai testato
reviews.summary: Tests the round Wilson on court and scores each shot, giving 10 out of 10 for the overhead, basic shot, low wall exit, block and smash, and 9.5 for the volley. Finds the sweet spot very wide, starting from the first row of holes, with impact feel around 6.8, medium hard leaning hard. Calls it the most powerful round racket they have tested, though below the Adidas Metalbone HRD in power. Suits advanced intermediate to advanced players who like a firmer touch. Calls the price still a little high.
reviews.more: Describes the specs as round shape, 3K carbon faces with a sanded finish, a firmer foam core, 26.5 balance and 365 g declared. Notes the cord alone adds 9 g and the mounted protector about 5 g more, so a weighed unit reads 375 to 378 g. Compares it with the Siux Electra Pro and Oxdog Sense Pro as polyvalent rackets with a little extra power. Adds that Wilson lowered prices while Babolat, Adidas and Nox raised theirs.
highlights: Finds the sweet spot very wide
most powerful round racket they have tested

reviews.keyPoint: Round racket with real power and a huge sweet spot.
reviews.stood: Very wide sweet spot and the most power they have tried in a round shape.
reviews.trade: Price is still a little high.
reviews.compared: Siux Electra Pro, Oxdog Sense Pro, Adidas Metalbone HRD

reviews.creator: Tino
reviews.summary: Switches from a Bullpadel Neuron to try this racket, curious after hearing it is strong for control. Finds it very good for controlling the ball, suited to a controlled baseline game that does not rely on attacks. Finds power a bit lacking compared with Head or Babolat models, so the body has to push the racket to generate pace. Calls the maneuverability light and the sweet spot wide. Notes the weight of 365 to 375 and a teardrop shape, so two to three hours of play is not tiring. Sees it as a fit for right-side players who build points for a left-side partner.
reviews.more: Compares the power with Head and Babolat rackets, where a light touch is enough to get pace, while here the player has to add their own push. Notes that a sharper attack needs more force from the player. Finds the racket fine for pure control play. Mentions the squarish tip makes the shape look like a diamond, though it is a teardrop. Suggests using it to give half balls so the left-side partner can finish the point.
highlights: very good for controlling the ball
two to three hours of play

reviews.stood: Very good ball control from the baseline with a wide sweet spot.
reviews.trade: Power is a bit lacking, so the player must push the racket.

reviews.creator: Justpadel
reviews.summary: Praises a forgiving contact area and a distinct upper power spot that gives very strong smashes. Finds the high balance does not feel excessively head-heavy. Struggles with overhead timing at first after using rounder rackets. Adapting brings an enthusiastic response and a 9.5 rating.
reviews.short: Praises a forgiving contact area and a distinct upper power spot that gives very strong smashes. Finds the high balance does not feel excessively head-heavy. Struggles with overhead timing at first after using rounder rackets. Adapting brings an enthusiastic response and a 9.5 rating.
reviews.keyPoint: Forgiving racket with a strong upper power spot.
reviews.stood: Forgiving contact area and very strong smashes from the upper power spot.
reviews.trade: Overhead timing takes time to adjust after rounder rackets.

reviews.creator: La Ruta del Padel
reviews.quote: Sentí que siempre le pegué bien
reviews.summary: Tests the Vertex 05 Geo 2026 and lists a weight of 365 to 375 g, a balance of 26 cm slightly towards the tip, a multieva core and rough 3D carbon faces. Finds the defence surprising for an offensive racket, crediting the 541 cm² hitting surface and 3K carbon with very high control. Feels well connected on every shot, even when accelerating with the wrist. Notes that the weight does not feel loaded in the tip, so acceleration is easy and the Geo technology adds extra pressure. Says the rough surface gives security and power on the bandeja, and the smash has good acceleration and spin. Rates it 10 out of 10.
highlights: rough surface gives security and power

reviews.keyPoint: Offensive racket that still defends with high control.
reviews.stood: Easy acceleration and high control, even in defence.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.quote: Es una pala de potencia fácil.
reviews.summary: Tests the Geo on court across baseline, volleys, overhead play and smashes, with the Gesacor removed to reach 353 g and a balance of 265 mm. Finds it more powerful than the standard Vertex, though a little below the new Neuron, with a medium-hard feel and a sweet spot placed in the medium-high zone. Rates the baseline play as decent for an attacking shape and the volleys as very complete. Likes the easy power on bandeja, vibora and smashes. Criticises the sandy rough finish missing from the logo area, which changes feel and slides the ball. Suits players who want easy power.
reviews.more: Compares it with the standard Vertex, calling it more progressive on fast blocking volleys because the ball does not get out of control. Removes the Gesacor and fits an overgrip to make it light, noting the medium-high balance can become demanding at a high weight. Expects the rough texture to wear down over time. Likes that the cord now exits from the centre of the cap. Notes the ball sinks slightly into the racket on flat smashes.
highlights: more powerful than the standard Vertex
easy power on bandeja, vibora and smashes
sandy rough finish missing from the logo

reviews.keyPoint: Easy power in an attacking shape.
reviews.stood: Easy power on bandeja, vibora and smashes without needing much effort.
reviews.trade: Rough texture is missing on the logo area, so feel and spin change.

reviews.creator: EverythingPadel
reviews.quote: This is the most powerful racket in the Vertex range
reviews.summary: Describes it as the most powerful racket in the Vertex range, thanks to a wide geometric face. Finds it head heavy with a firm feel, a wider sweet spot and a rough sandpaper surface. Notes the Geo uses 3K carbon, which leads to a stiffer, firmer feel. Recommends it for players who want to play super attacking. Places it at the attacking end of the Vertex range, ahead of the normal Vertex and the control based Vertex Hybrid. Prefers the Hybrid models personally. Hears a second player call it lightweight and maneuverable, though that player picks the Hack for extra comfort and control.
reviews.more: Compares it with the normal Vertex, which is more balanced between power and control with a medium feel. Calls the Vertex Hybrid the most control based of the three, with a round head and a massive sweet spot. Lists the Curve Active technology as shared across the Vertex range and meant to add maneuverability. Sees the Neuron Edge as similar because it also uses a wide geometric face. Ranks it just below the Explode for power across the Bullpadel range.
highlights: most powerful racket in the Vertex range
head heavy with a firm feel

reviews.keyPoint: Most powerful Vertex, built for attacking players.
reviews.stood: Wide geometric face gives the most power in the Vertex range.
reviews.trade: Head heavy and firm, less suited to control based players.
reviews.compared: Bullpadel Vertex, Bullpadel Vertex Hybrid, Bullpadel Hack, Bullpadel Neuron Edge, Bullpadel Explode

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: La Geo es más explosiva, definitivamente sí se siente algo más agresiva
reviews.summary: Compares the Geo with the standard Vertex 05 2026 in every court zone, using a 364 g unit with 26.2 cm balance against a 370 g Vertex. Finds the Geo slightly more head-heavy, a bit harder than the Vertex, and more reactive, with the ball leaving faster. Gives the Vertex the point at the baseline for handling and sweet spot, calls the volley and the bandeja ties, and awards the smash to the Geo as more powerful. Notes the smooth glossy finish around the Bullpadel logo could make the hand slip. Calls it a versatile racket leaning slightly toward attack, not a super offensive one.
reviews.more: Finds the Geo easier for gaining speed on the bandeja, but more likely to end up in the back glass, rating its good bandejas around eight and a half with more errors, against seven and a half for the Vertex. Says the Vertex rough sandy surface grips the ball well when new. Compares the Geo reactivity with a Metalbone, which is more of a cannon. Suggests the Geo for above medium hardness and easier attack, and the Vertex for a dry feel and speed control.
highlights: more reactive, with the ball leaving faster
awards the smash to the Geo
reviews.short: Compares the Geo with the standard Vertex 05 2026 in every court zone, using a 364 g unit with 26.2 cm balance against a 370 g Vertex. Finds the Geo slightly more head-heavy, a bit harder than the Vertex, and more reactive, with the ball leaving faster. Gives the Vertex the point at the baseline for handling and sweet spot, calls the volley and the bandeja ties, and awards the smash to the Geo as more powerful. Notes the smooth glossy finish around the Bullpadel logo could make the hand slip. Calls it a versatile racket leaning slightly toward attack, not a super offensive one.
reviews.keyPoint: Slightly more powerful and reactive than the standard Vertex.
reviews.stood: Easier to attack with and a bit more powerful in the smash.
reviews.trade: Less manageable than the Vertex and more errors on the bandeja.
reviews.compared: Bullpadel Vertex 05, Adidas Metalbone, Bullpadel Explora

reviews.creator: PadelLab
reviews.quote: esta paleta despida un poco más rápido
reviews.summary: Compares the Vertex Geo 2026 with the standard Vertex 05 2026 and describes the Geo as similar but with a bit more power. Puts the balance at around 25.3 to 25.4 cm, higher than the other model, and notes it rises further if the removable core piece is taken off. Finds the face harder and the feel drier, so power shots like the smash, the wall hook and the víbora leave faster. Says the back of the court asks for more push and a longer finish, while the net is easier. Recommends it to players moving from a hybrid or control racket who want more power.
reviews.more: Notes the standard Vertex 05 2026 has a medium balance of 25.1 to 25.2 cm and a medium feel. Says both rackets widen the heart of the frame to cut vibration, which lowers the balance a little. Adds that both come with removable shockouts, which can be moved to change the balance. Explains that softer rackets send the ball out more on slow shots and less on fast ones.
highlights: moving from a hybrid or control racket

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: sicuramente non è una palla che fa i buchi per terra
reviews.summary: Tests the racket on court across baseline play, volleys, lobs and smashes. Finds the feel medium hard to hard, yet very comfortable, with strong control and no arm fatigue or vibration despite a not especially light weight. Calls handling excellent and the sweet spot far from small for a racket of this type. Rates the rough surface as giving very incisive spin. Finds power lacking, with smashes less explosive than a classic Vertex, so it is not for serial hitters. Sees it suiting right or left side players, and possibly an intermediate moving toward advanced. Likes the strap now exiting from the centre, which no longer twists.
reviews.more: Notes the name is Vertex but the feel differs from the old style, with less free ball exit and more arm needed in defence. Finds lobs rise well and transitions from defence to attack work nicely. Points out the custom weight system adding up to 9 g in three spots, and the Exacor grip remains. Gives marks of 9 for control and 8 for sweet spot and vibrations. Feels the racket looks tough and unlikely to chip easily, and asks players to confirm.
highlights: less explosive than a classic Vertex

reviews.quote: una pala bastante polivalente, que es una pala muy manejable
reviews.summary: Tests it for one week on court and finds a versatile hybrid shaped racket with a medium to medium hard feel, a little firmer than last year's regular Vertex. Notes a medium low balance, measured at 25 cm, and finds it very easy to handle from the back of the court. Finds the volley is where its full potential shows, with bandeja and vibora also working well, and says smashes work with good technique. Warns that hitting too high on the face kills the ball. Dislikes the high price, the finish and the sandy texture that wears off within a week. Suggests it for intermediate to advanced players who want one racket that does most things.
reviews.more: Compares the feel to last year's regular Vertex and places it one or two points firmer. Puts it between the Babolat Viper and Veron, closer to the Veron, with the Viper drier and the Veron about half a point harder. Adds that the Veron was tried in summer heat, so the gap may shrink in winter. Notes that lobs need a longer swing, while balls off the back wall work well. Says the bridge triangle is slightly larger than in earlier years.

reviews.creator: PADELREVIEW ENG
reviews.quote: it's really a great rocket
reviews.summary: Tests the first Bullpadel racket signed by Pablo Cardona on court, after comparing it with the earlier Ionic Power. Finds a full carbon racket with a medium hard feel, more reactive than the standard Vertex, giving extra ball speed in fast rallies without losing control. Rates the sweet spot as not huge but precise, in the upper middle area, and notes that a miss is felt at once. Calls it more demanding than the Ionic Power, with less free power but more manoeuvrable and precise. Suggests it for left side or left handed players, upper intermediate to pro, who attack. Finds the price high but calls it a great racket.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Ionic Power, which was not carbon, was heavier and gave more ball output and easier power. Places the Geo as the choice for more advanced players. Lists the weight at 365 g, inside a range they call perfect at 365 to 375, and the balance at 25.6 cm, medium. Notes that the new vertex bridge raises stiffness and that vibration is reduced.
highlights: extra ball speed in fast rallies

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: Indubbiamente è una racchetta esplosiva.
reviews.summary: Tests it over several hours of play and finds an explosive diamond that is lighter and easier to move than expected. Weighs 362 g without the Exacor grip and 369 g with it, at a 25.5 cm balance. Gives power a 9 and calls the sweet spot relatively generous for the shape. Finds spin technical, improving once the glossy logo area wears down. Rates the volley a 9 and enjoys the flat smash most. Says it needs rhythm and arm speed, and suits advanced intermediate players. Calls the price a little high.
reviews.more: Compares it with the standard Vertex 05, finding that one grips and spins better while this one is more explosive and has a slightly more central sweet spot. Says the Babolat Counter Viper has easier ball output, but this has more power up high. Calls it more of a power diamond than a hybrid. Notes the upper part of the face works less well, and forced spin on the vibora shot tends to fly straighter. Suggests removing the Exacor and fitting a traditional grip.

reviews.trade: Needs rhythm and arm speed, so not for lower intermediate players.

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.quote: tiras muy bien la bola donde quieres
reviews.summary: Tests it on court zone by zone, from defence to smash, against the standard Vertex. Finds control the main strength at every pace, with a dry feel and a slightly higher ball exit at fast pace. Rates the sweet spot as standard size, medium high on the face, and notes the ball gets shorter when struck off centre. Calls power only moderate, not the strongest in the Bullpadel range, and says a medium good smash technique is needed. Dislikes the sandy texture only on parts of the face, which can let the ball float. Weighs in at 363 g without the hesacore. Suits players who like to accelerate and play firm.
reviews.more: Compares it with the normal Vertex. Finds it slightly harder, a bit more reactive and with a touch more weight in the head, so volleys ask for more attention. Says the ball leaves faster at the same effort, making it more offensive. Places it below the Xplo and Neuron 02 for power, and says the ST4 and Metalbone Hard give more rebound for less effort. Ranks the zones as bandeja and vibora first, then volley, smash and defence. Finds the normal Vertex 05 slightly more comfortable this year than in earlier years.
highlights: not the strongest in the Bullpadel range

reviews.trade: Needs decent smash technique and gives only moderate power.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: la raquette, elle vibre moins et elle est plus stable
reviews.summary: Compares the Geo head to head with the classic Vertex 05 2026, measuring it at 370 g with a 258 mm balance, lower than the 263 mm of the classic. Notes the 3K carbon and a more angular diamond shape, aimed at more tolerance. Feels comfort and stability first: the racket vibrates less, gives more touch in defence and makes lobs and low balls at the feet easier. Finds smashes leave with much less speed, so the legs must be fully engaged. Reports a gain in control and precision on high shots. Recommends it for players at level 5 and above who want power with control.
reviews.more: Rates the classic Vertex 05 2026 as more reactive and clearly more powerful than the 2025 model, with a balance of 263 mm against 251, but much less forgiving off centre. Picks the Geo if forced to choose, finding it easier to play and much less tiring over time. Sees it as suited to building the point and pushing opponents into errors. Calls it power oriented despite its comfort, so level 5 minimum. Advises trying both before buying.

reviews.keyPoint: Comfortable, stable diamond racket that gives up some smash power.
reviews.stood: Comfort, stability and precise control on high shots, with less vibration.
reviews.trade: Smashes leave much slower, so the legs must be fully engaged.

reviews.creator: Padel5
reviews.quote: Es una pala directa, seca, con muchísima potencia y sin concesiones.
reviews.summary: Tests the Pablo Cardona model for 2026 and finds a direct, dry racket with a lot of power and no concessions. Calls it a cannon on smashes, where the ball rises or can be brought down without full effort, but it does not help if the ball is not hit centred. Finds volleys very firm, with no vibration, though a soft contact falls short. Rates bandejas as very heavy and easy to keep deep, while touch shots and dead balls demand more technique. Calls defence its most demanding area, since it is not agile or soft. Suits attacking players who want to close points and press at the net.
reviews.more: Finds the rulos to the fence work well if the technique is right. Says the racket does not grip the ball much, but with arm speed and spin the ball bounces where wanted and troubles the opponent. Notes that defence needs good leg work and good reading of the point to avoid being caught out. Says it is for players who live off attack, and not for anyone wanting comfort or extra help in defence.
highlights: close points and press at the net

reviews.trade: Demanding in defence and unforgiving when the ball is not hit centred.

reviews.creator: The Padel School
reviews.quote: A lot of effortless power it feels like on this racket.
reviews.summary: Compares the Geo with the standard Vertex 05 and tests it in defense and at the net. Notes a 3K carbon build, 365 to 375 g weight and a balance towards the top, which favours a more offensive player. Finds a slightly larger sweet spot, more rebound and extra forgiveness off centre from the geo shape. Feels a lot of effortless power on the racket. Feels comfortable in defense, easy to maneuver, with good control on chiquitas and when defending the glass. Gets good pop on volleys and aggressive overheads. Recommends the Vertex range from intermediate level up.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Vertex 05, which uses 12K carbon, feels firmer in the face and has a lower balance. Finds the Vertex 05 gives less power and rebound, especially on overheads and aggressive volleys, though it stays forgiving and controllable. Notes both rackets share a vibration reducing technology and the same grip to put less strain on the arm. Calls the Vertex 05 an excellent all round racket and the Geo a bit more powerful with a bigger surface area.

reviews.keyPoint: Forgiving offensive all rounder with extra power and rebound.
reviews.stood: Larger sweet spot and effortless power while staying easy to control and maneuver.
reviews.trade: Favours a more offensive player, while the Vertex 05 suits all round play.

reviews.creator: Setup Padel | Mario Pazos
reviews.quote: Es una pala que puede jugar totalmente ofensivo o totalmente defensivo
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Vertex 05 Geo on court after going through its parts one by one. Finds it a touch harder and more aggressive than the standard Vertex 05, thanks to 3K carbon, while keeping the versatility. Reports a balance of 26 cm, which they call medium, and says the shock-out weights shrink the sweet spot. Calls it comfortable and easy to move, with a standard sweet spot that felt slightly smaller. Rates the smash as the biggest positive, with the bandeja and vibora good once adapted. Dislikes the smooth carbon area near the hitting zone, where the ball slips a little. Suits Vertex players who want more bite without losing versatility.
reviews.more: Places it between the standard Vertex 05 and the Hack 04 in aggression. Expects the 3K carbon to hold its stiffness longer, since the 12K carbon of the standard Vertex turns softer as the foam wears. Says removing the shock-out weights makes it lighter and raises the balance slightly. Dislikes the Exacor grip option and notes the rough finish lasts only two or three months. Mentions it is a Pablo Cardona signature model and hard to find because it is new.
highlights: a touch harder and more aggressive
shock-out weights shrink the sweet spot

reviews.stood: Smash gains extra bite while the racket stays comfortable and versatile.
reviews.trade: Needs some adaptation and has a slightly reduced sweet spot because of the shock-out weights.

reviews.creator: Padel Smash TV
reviews.quote: you get a lot of control on it
reviews.summary: Tests it on court with two players and lists a teardrop shape, 360 to 375 g and a 38 mm profile. Calls it the best looking racket in the AT10 line. Finds the 12K firmer than the 18K, with one player calling it a little hard when hitting. Reports a lot of control but limited power, so players need to put some muscle behind the ball. Feels comfortable in defence and in volleys at the net, with a balance that suits a style leaning to the top. Rates the AT10 range as versatile rackets for advanced or high intermediate players.
highlights: best looking racket in the AT10 line
a lot of control but limited power
put some muscle behind the ball

reviews.creator: Tom Pandore
reviews.quote: La maniabilité est vraiment incroyable.
reviews.summary: Tests the 12K 2026 version as a level 7-8 player, on a 375 g racket with low balance and a hard Black Eva foam. Finds the handling incredible, the sweet spot wide and the feel firm but comfortable. Notes easy power from plenty of assistance, which makes the ball fly out and causes errors when rushing in match play. Rates smashes, kick smashes and the vibora as working well, and spin as very good thanks to the 3D texture and sanding. Calls it versatile and tolerant, suited from P100 players up to advanced ones.
reviews.more: Plays it on both the right and left sides and finds it works for calm or aggressive styles. Feels the assistance is higher than the rigidity suggests, so players with strong raw power may find it holds them back. Warns that the ball can shoot out when rushing, which gives errors on attacks. Plans to keep playing with it rather than sell it, since it fits the need for a hard, very manoeuvrable racket, but the assistance remains a question.
highlights: easy power from plenty of assistance

reviews.stood: Incredible handling with a wide sweet spot and comfortable feel.
reviews.trade: Assistance can send balls out too fast in match play.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.quote: Es una pala que yo este año la catalogaría de potencia fácil.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 hybrid with HR3 Black EVA rubber and aluminised 12K carbon, set up with 2 g weights for a 255 mm balance from a stock 252 mm. Finds it more reactive and bouncy at medium and low speeds, with easy ball exit and a very agile feel. Notes the new double rough texture gives clearly more spin and grip than the 2025 model. Loses control and precision at high pace, especially off the sweet spot, and feels less predictable than the 2025 12K. Rates it as easy power rather than pure power. Suits players wanting help moving the ball with little effort.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 18K 2026, which gives more control from the baseline at a high rhythm, while the 12K moves the ball more easily at medium speeds. Prefers last year's MLD rubber for control and pure power at high speeds. Notes that the 4 g red weights give a 257 mm balance and over 370 g, which makes the racket more demanding. Calls the sweet spot slightly smaller than on the 18K and more centred. Plans a three-way comparison with the 18K and the Edu Alonso Ventus.
highlights: control and precision at high pace
easy power rather than pure power
