reviews.stood: Easy ball exit and agility at medium and low speeds, plus better spin.
reviews.trade: Less control and precision at high pace, especially off the sweet spot.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 Genius 18K 2026, Nox AT10 Genius 12K 2025, Nox Ventus Edu Alonso

reviews.creator: Super Padel Bros
reviews.quote: Ho apprezzato molto il comfort di questa pala.
reviews.summary: Tests it on court in cold weather, around 7 to 8 degrees, with deflated balls, and calls it a good racket that does not justify the price. Finds the comfort very high, with no vibrations, an arm that never tires and a very agile feel. Likes the generous sweet spot and good spin from the light rough surface. Criticises the weak ball exit, low power and an unclear touch that costs precision at the net and on overheads. Gives 7.5 for the net, 7.5 for overheads and 8 for smashes. Suggests it for beginners up to intermediate players.
reviews.more: Notes the 2026 weight balance system, where adhesive weights of 2 to 5 g can go on the head. Gives the balance at 25.4, dropping a little with overgrip, and sees the shape as round rather than teardrop. Finds the rubber soft and not really black, which makes the ball sink into the face. Struggles with timing on overheads at first because of the low balance and light head. Mentions liking the 2025 18K and the 2023 AT10, and dismisses the 2024 as senseless.

reviews.keyPoint: Comfortable and agile but overpriced for its performance.
reviews.stood: Very comfortable and agile, with no vibrations and good spin.
reviews.trade: Weak ball exit and low power, and not worth the price.

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: Una pala tecnica, secca, precisa, che richiede qualità
reviews.summary: Tests it on both sides of the court, removing the stock custom grip and using an overgrip instead. Finds the feel dry and firm, with fast ball exit, good handling at the net and a surface that gives plenty of spin on volleys. Scores power, control and handling at 9 each. Calls the sweet spot not generous, so clean, centred contact is needed. Finds defensive recovery from awkward balls harder than attacking play. Dislikes the custom grip and the price. Says it needs an advanced player, especially on the right side, and rewards good technique.
reviews.more: Explains that the racket has a teardrop shape, 12K Alum Xtrem carbon faces and an H3 Black EVA core, which is a middle ground leaning hard. Notes a weight balance system that lets players add or remove weights to move balance toward the head or the handle. Lists a weight of 360 to 375 g and a 38 mm thickness. Finds the response as consistent as the 18K version of last year, not erratic as in some earlier years. Mentions an Italian market version with a tricolour flag. Says an advanced intermediate may manage it on the left.
reviews.short: Tests it on both sides of the court, removing the stock custom grip and using an overgrip instead. reviews.keyPoint: Technical, dry racket that rewards clean centred contact.
reviews.stood: Dry, precise feel with strong spin and handling at the net.
reviews.trade: Small sweet spot, weaker defensive recovery and a high price.

reviews.creator: Setup Padel
reviews.quote: es una pala de notable, alto en casi todo
reviews.summary: Tests the 12K aluminised version on court after going through its specs, noting 365 g with overgrip and a 26 cm balance. Finds the ball output controlled and comfortable, with the viper and bandeja standing out and the volley harder to speed up. Calls it a medium-hardness racket that barely changed across temperatures, with a standard sweet spot and very easy handling. Warns that it is not a pure power racket despite Tapia's name on it. Rates it an eight in everything and recommends it to intermediate and advanced players, not beginners. Criticises the chromic paint and the high price.
reviews.more: Compares it with last year's 18K, which they played for a long time and felt was missing something, and says the 12K supplies it. Finds the change from EOS Flap to EOS Tunnel unnoticeable and the 3D rough finish slightly sandy, wanting a more marked texture for spin. Notes the aluminised carbon kept the feel steady between roughly 8 and 16 degrees.
reviews.short: Tests the 12K aluminised version on court after going through its specs, noting 365 g with overgrip and a 26 cm balance. Finds the ball output controlled and comfortable, with the viper and bandeja standing out and the volley harder to speed up. Calls it a medium-hardness racket that barely changed across temperatures, with a standard sweet spot and very easy handling. Warns that it is not a pure power racket despite Tapia's name on it. Rates it an eight in everything and recommends it to intermediate and advanced players, not beginners. Criticises the chromic paint and the high price.
reviews.keyPoint: Versatile racket that shines on viper and bandeja.
reviews.stood: Controlled, comfortable ball output and very good viper and bandeja confidence.
reviews.trade: Not a pure power racket, expensive, and too technical for beginners.

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas
reviews.quote: La tocas más despacio y aún así la bola sale con velocidad.
reviews.summary: Compares the white 12K Extreme with HR3 Black EVA rubber against the black 18K in a head to head on court. Measures 362 g and a balance of 25.5 on the 12K, and finds it easy to move with a good, centred sweet spot. Rates it as the more reactive of the two, so speed comes easily on the smash and bandeja. Finds it harder to control on blocks and volleys, where the ball can fly long into the glass. Calls it very easy to extract power from, and picks the 18K as winner by a small margin. Warns that players coming from less bouncy rackets need to adapt.
reviews.more: Notes the 12K shell is stiffer than the 18K, yet the HR3 rubber returns the ball faster at low and medium speed. Places its hardness slightly below a Neuron. Feels it soften a little on full power smashes, and calls the smash a tie between both rackets. Adds that tip weights would make it even better there.
highlights: harder to control on blocks and volleys
very easy to extract power from

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: c'est une super raquette au niveau de la volée
reviews.summary: Tests the 12K Alum Xtrem against the 18K and 12K Light versions with lab measurements and court play. Measures it at 363 g with a 266 mm balance and 64 RA stiffness, the stiffest of the three. Finds it well balanced and manoeuvrable in defence, with a touch that makes chiquitas and lobs easy to control. Rates it a real treat at the net, with a lot of reactivity and precision. Calls it the clear winner in the smash power test. Warns that the sweet spot is demanding when hits go off centre. Recommends it for advanced to expert players ranked 5000 or higher.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 18K, which feels more comfortable and tolerant but gave more faults on high shots and less control. Finds the 12K Light the most manoeuvrable but the least powerful, needing more leg work. Notes the new weight balance system on the frame edge, with supplied strips of 2 g and 4 g that can bring a racket at the top of the weight range to 383 g. Says it gives similar feelings to the Adidas Metalbone at the net.
highlights: well balanced and manoeuvrable in defence
clear winner in the smash power test

reviews.creator: Mejora Tu Padel
reviews.quote: es una pala muy fácil de usar desde el primer momento que la agarréis
reviews.summary: Compares it with four other hybrid rackets for 2026 and calls it one of the easiest rackets on the market. Describes a 12K aluminised carbon face with an HR3 Black EVA core that feels medium hardness, slightly firmer than the standard HR3, and a very manageable sweet spot close to the hand. Notes the frame takes 2 g weight plates that change balance but not the sweet spot, so leverage stays the same. Points to the Attack version for more leverage. Finds it too soft at times when pushed, though it suits players who want an easy defence without losing punch.
reviews.more: Rates it as the easiest racket to recommend and calls it the best selling racket in the world. Says it does not lift them as much as it lifts Tapia, yet it behaves well from the first grip. Finds it softer than the Fuji and the Vertex Geo, which have noticeably more hardness. Compares it with the EA10, which has a sweet spot even closer to the hand and less overhead power. Describes the white and gold finish as very attractive.

change balance but not the sweet spot

Measures 355 g without accessories against 368 g on the box, balance 25.5. Notes the head feels empty, so the arm must work on lifted shots and volleys sink the ball when hit harder. Likes the bandeja and kick smash at medium to medium high pace. Calls the finish poor, with crooked decals and paint bubbles, and rates value a 4. Suits intermediate and upper intermediate players, less so advanced ones.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 18K 2025, which gets the main recommendation for more ball output and a livelier feel. Grants the 12K more control. Finds the Raptor Plus offers a bit more feel and activity at slow pace, at a lower price. Describes the 12K Alum Xtrem as a possible option for right side players once the price drops. Notes the weight came in 13 g under the box figure.

reviews.quote: La miglior tapia di sempre
reviews.summary: Tests the racket on court from the baseline, at the net and on overhead shots, then scores each area. Finds it drier and faster off the face than last year's version, with a firmer 12K carbon face and HR3 Black Eva rubber. Calls it very maneuverable and controlled, with good feel for touch shots, but not a cannon. Notes the sweet spot is not wide, so precision is needed. Weighs it at 365 g with a medium to high balance. Gives scores of 8 to 8.5 in most areas, with 7 for sweet spot and 6 for value. Places it at upper intermediate to advanced level, for either side of the court.
reviews.more: Tries the weight system with two 2 g adhesive weights, which makes the racket heavier and the balance higher, and prefers it without them. Says the stickers do not damage the paint but take time to fit. Calls the yearly price increases too much. Finds the net game easy for tricks and touch, and says the ball rarely escapes on overheads.

versatile rather than a maximum-power racket

reviews.quote: es una pala para mí muy polivalente
reviews.summary: Goes through the specs first, then tests it on court in defence, volleys, overhead play and smashes. Finds it very comfortable, with a medium feel and a balance that is not high, so it does not feel heavy. Rates control and ball feel as the strong points for blocks, volleys and directing the ball. Notes the double rough surface grips spin well. Wants a little more power for aggression and feels the teardrop shape does not help the rulo. Calls it a hybrid profile that delivers but is not aggressive. Suits players with several years of play, given the investment, and points to an Edu Alonso model for more power.
reviews.more: Explains the changes from the previous model: an HR3 Black Eva core, 12K carbon instead of 18K, a longer handle, a Maestrap strap system, the EOS holes and weight slots to alter the balance. Expects the aluminised Xtrem face to add rigidity and a more even feel in hot or cold weather. Expects it to be a best seller this year. Suggests the red Edu Alonso racket for a more compact hit and more power.

reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Alum Xtrem across defence, viper and bandeja, volley and smash, comparing it with last year's AT10 12K and the 2024 one. Finds a harder carbon and HR3 Black EVA rubber that give more ball speed for the same effort, and a very manageable racket with a slightly more centred sweet spot. Notes less control at fast pace, balls that fly to the wall more easily, and a need to pull the tip down. Ranks viper and bandeja first, then volley, defence and smash. Rates it as a good fit for players wanting extra help in attack with medium technique or above, less for those wanting control.
reviews.more: Describes the changes: a stiffer aluminised 12K Xtrem carbon, HR3 Black EVA once used in limited edition AT2 LTD models, and a matte double rough finish. Finds the new surface grips spin better on the smash por tres and lets volleys carry more weight. Points to the Edu Alonso versions for a drier, more controlled feel closer to the 2024 model. Notes an October release is expected. Notes the smash tests were done in wind with used balls.

Compares average distance over 10 smashes per racket and finds power clearly above the 18K and close to the 2025 12K. Notes it needs more self-generated speed on bandejas and víboras, and that spin help is about the same. Rates it 9.25 in every aspect, suited to players wanting a balanced racket rather than a very hard one.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 12K and finds more control and better feel, but slightly less power. Notes the changes: HR3 Black EVA rubber replaces MLD Black EVA, 12K aluminized carbon replaces the 18K, and the new mold allows lead strips at the tip to raise balance. Says the aluminized carbon keeps performance steady across temperatures. Warns that anyone seeking a really hard, all power racket has better alternatives. Finds it a little more technically demanding than the 2025 models, but nothing extreme.

Describes the 18K as the more controlled, precise and quick racket with a slightly wider sweet spot and easier ball output, but with less push when driving. Notes the two use different rubbers and a differently woven carbon. Calls both versatile rackets for a wide audience, with the choice depending on wanting speed and feel or a fuller, more aggressive racket.

Reports the 18K gives more rubber feel at low pace, while the 12K Extreme feels fuller in attack and a bit more aggressive.

Likes it much more at the net, where volleys come out flatter and easier to place. Calls the bandeja and víbora fast and controlled, and the smash very good, with depth and spin. Describes it as a real cannon with a lot of control.
reviews.more: Likes it slightly more than the Explo for bandeja, víbora and smash, though would pick its smaller sister for defence. Finds it a little more attacking than the earlier racket tested, with the ball leaving sharper because of the higher balance. Points to the new Prince Block prisms around the frame, 3K carbon faces, a slightly longer handle and an improved air system for handling. Thinks it could sit in the top three Bullpadel rackets this year.

reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Neuron 02 Edge with and without dampeners, preferring it without. Finds a dry, semi-hard feel with 3K carbon and multi EVA rubber, more attack than last year but a slightly higher balance and less handling. Dislikes the small sweet spot in the middle and the split between glossy and matte areas, which changes ball feel at high pace. Notes vibration and instability on off-centre hits. Recommends it for high levels and offensive net players with a long technical swing, but says it gives no help on defence or power.
reviews.more: Calls it more versatile than the previous year's model, with a lot of control and a little extra power, but not a power racket. Criticises brands that make the logo glossy and the rest matte. Calls it a good, complete racket, but not an easy one.

reviews.quote: la palla veramente la metti dove vuoi tu
reviews.summary: Plays it for several days from the right side, after getting little from the 2025 Neuron on the left. Finds control and precision excellent, comfort excellent with zero vibrations, and the racket agile despite a medium high balance. Calls the power manageable rather than maximum, and the spin good but below expectations. Notes it needs faster ball speeds to activate, so rules out beginners. Gives 8.5 for baseline, net play, shots from above and smashes, with the flat smash the biggest surprise. Measures 369 g including the Hesacore grip.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 Neuron, which offered control and comfort but gave little from the left side. Finds the Edge works as a finishing racket as well, not only for building play. Dislikes the Hesacore grip as too thick for a medium to small hand. Rates the sweet spot as medium, neither generous nor severe. Finds the touch dry and honest, with modest ball exit that needs some arm. Calls the volley solid and stable, and the smash kick weaker because of limited spin.

Loves the touch at the net and finds smashes work well with good technique. Calls it versatile and notes the sweet spot is not bad. Finds the price high. Recommends it to intermediate to advanced players who want some extra power.

reviews.summary: Tests the racket on court after liking last season's classic Neuron, and finds it slightly more manageable but still a muscular, demanding option. Rates control as the main strength, with a hard feel that lets them judge force precisely and push hard without errors. Likes the vibora most, whether flat or worked, and finds volleys incisive. Finds the lob needs to be pushed, ball output limited, sweet spot average and vibrations noticeable on the arm after long sessions. Calls it suited to intermediate to advanced players, a bit more to the left side, and gives it 8.25 overall.
reviews.more: Compares it with last season's classic Neuron, calling it a little less demanding but still needing a strong, intense player. Suggests the ergonomic grip can be kept or removed, knowing it changes balance. Notes the custom system adds 3, 6 or 9 g to shift balance. Finds it works on both sides: on the right it suits a muscular, intense player, on the left it gives more finishing power. Warns that players prone to elbow pain should think twice.

reviews.quote: Una racchetta per giocatori offensivi veramente di destra, molto esplosiva.
reviews.summary: Tests the Milano Premier Padel version on court with a partner from the baseline, at the net and on overheads, then scores each shot. Finds it explosive from the back of the court and calls it a racket for aggressive right-side players. Notes the sweet spot is small, so the ball dies at the net when hit badly, and slow rallies are where it struggles. Weighs 371 g with the Hexacore grip and 26 cm balance, and finds it moves well despite the weight. Suggests removing the Hexacore and using two overgrips. Gives power 8.5 and value 6.
reviews.more: Prefers the racket without the Hexacore, saying it makes the racket less offensive and that removing it would cut weight and raise balance. Finds block volleys can stay short when hit badly. Struggles most on the x3 smash because of the timing lost moving the racket, while flat smashes and the vibora work well. Gives smash and vibora 8.5, control 7.5 and maneuverability 7.5. Notes the Milano version is sold only in Italy.
highlights: explosive from the back of the court
removing the Hexacore and using two overgrips
reviews.short: Tests the Milano Premier Padel version on court with a partner from the baseline, at the net and on overheads, then scores each shot. Finds it explosive from the back of the court and calls it a racket for aggressive right-side players. Notes the sweet spot is small, so the ball dies at the net when hit badly, and slow rallies are where it struggles. Weighs 371 g with the Hexacore grip and 26 cm balance, and finds it moves well despite the weight. Suggests removing the Hexacore and using two overgrips. Gives power 8.5 and value 6.
reviews.keyPoint: Explosive, heavy racket that rewards clean contact.
reviews.stood: Very explosive from the baseline and strong on smashes and vibora.
reviews.trade: Small sweet spot and heavy, so it struggles on slow rallies and mishits.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.quote: Ostras, que sorprende con el juego aéreo porque se siente potente.
reviews.summary: Compares the Edge version of the 2026 Neuron 02 with the standard Neuron 02 on court, in baseline play, volleys and overheads. Finds the Edge has a diamond shape and a 261 mm balance, against 250 mm for the standard model, with the same 365 g weight and 3K carbon. Rates the touch as medium hard and dry on both. Calls the Edge more powerful, especially on smashes, volleys and the viper, and surprising for how well it works in attack. Finds the standard version more controllable and manoeuvrable from the baseline. Suggests the Edge for players who want to hit hard.
reviews.more: Finds the Edge best at the net, calling it one of the 2026 Bullpadel rackets they like most for volleys, though fast blocks need care with impact points. Says the sweet spot is standard size and the ball travels less when hitting off centre. Notes the Edge feels a little harder than the previous Neuron. Says the standard version resembles the 2025 Neuron and suits players who want control with versatility. Adds that both use a multi-EVA rubber with softer outer layers and four Easy Vibes.
highlights: diamond shape and a 261 mm balance
medium hard and dry on both
more controllable and manoeuvrable from the baseline

reviews.keyPoint: Clearly more powerful than the standard version at the net.
reviews.stood: Easy power on smashes, volleys and viper, surprising for its shape.
reviews.trade: Less control and manoeuvrability than the standard version from the baseline.

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.quote: Como digo, posiblemente la pala más potente de Bullpadel este año.
reviews.summary: Tests it on court in defence, mid court, volleys and smashes, using it with and without the Hesacore. Finds a medium-hard racket with a standard sweet spot that punishes off-centre hits, since balls come out shorter. Rates control as very good even when playing firm, with a little more attacking help than the Bullpadel Xplo or Hack. Calls it possibly the most powerful Bullpadel of the year, though it needs a medium to good technical level. Likes it most for the viper and bandeja zone. Recommends it for players who push the ball and extend shots, not for those wanting easy rebound.
reviews.more: Compares it with the previous Neuron and finds more hardness, more balance and a stiffer feel, so the switch is worthwhile for players wanting a more offensive racket. Points to the hybrid Neuron 02 for better maneuverability and less attacking response. Prefers it with the Hesacore removed, which takes off 15 g and moves the balance from 26 to 26.4 cm. Finds the Xplo softened faster with use, and says a Metalbone Hard gives power more easily through higher rebound.
highlights: most powerful Bullpadel of the year

reviews.stood: Very good control with extra attacking response when playing firm.
reviews.trade: Balls come out short off the sweet spot, and it offers little rebound help.
reviews.compared: Bullpadel Vertex, Bullpadel Xplo, Bullpadel Hack, Adidas Metalbone Hard, Bullpadel Neuron 02, Bullpadel Neuron (previous year)

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: El control de las velocidades me parece sublime
reviews.summary: Tests the Neuron Edge on court after trying most of the Bullpadel range, with a racket weighing 364 g and a balance of 25.8 cm. Finds it medium hard with a dry feel, good control over ball speed and solid, stable contact, but little reactivity, so it needs more effort and a technique from mid court forward. Rates the volley as the best zone, with control described as sublime. Finds the sweet spot standard and the smash powerful on flat shots, though the head is slow to drop. Dislikes the Gesacor and calls the price high. Suits players who want control over speed rather than explosive power.
reviews.more: Notes a redesigned mould with angular polygonal frames, a multi-EVA core in soft, hard, soft layers and air channels for agility. Welcomes the string now exiting through the middle of the cap across the range. Believes removing the Gesacor would raise the balance and make the smash and viper more aggressive, though weight would drop. Suggests a matte rough finish would grip the ball more. Expects the less reactive feel to cost effort in the Spanish winter, but likes it in warmer seasons.
highlights: medium hard with a dry feel
Rates the volley as the best zone

reviews.keyPoint: Controlled, stable, hard racket for players who push forward.
reviews.stood: Control over ball speed at the net, with a solid and stable feel.
reviews.trade: Low reactivity, so it takes effort to move the ball.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.summary: Prefers the Edge for its higher contact zone, firmer attacking volleys and more accessible smash power. Finds it still gives useful precision and tolerance. Notes faster defensive returns can surprise opponents. Says it needs a little adaptation and sufficient technique. Calls the standard Neuron the easier-handling option at the net.
reviews.short: Prefers the Edge for its higher contact zone, firmer attacking volleys and more accessible smash power. Finds it still gives useful precision and tolerance. reviews.keyPoint: Higher contact zone brings firmer volleys and easier smashes.
reviews.stood: Higher contact zone, firmer attacking volleys and more accessible smash power.
reviews.trade: Needs some adaptation and technique; the standard Neuron handles more easily at the net.

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: È davvero una pala che mi soddisfa veramente tanto.
reviews.summary: Tests the diamond-shaped racket at a Rome club, noting a multilayer Multieva core, 3K carbon faces and balance at 26 cm. Rates volleys 8.5, basic shots 9, high wall exit 9, smash 9 and block 8. Calls power good but never maximum, and finds the sweet spot smaller than last year's model, so hits must be more central. Feels some vibration on blocks despite the shock-outs. Suits intermediate, advanced and semi-professional players, and says it takes several sessions to get used to the core.
reviews.more: Compares it with last year's Neuron, finding the racket feels harder now, where the older one was softer and gave a standard feel. Finds more power from the Multieva core but a smaller sweet spot than the older model. Feels soft touch stays comfortable, while pushing harder brings more power. Suggests it may suit Fede Chingotto, who hits flatter, but doubts other professionals would use it. Advises trying it before buying and playing it several times. Calls the price too high and urges the brand to lower it.
highlights: sweet spot smaller than last year's model
takes several sessions to get used

reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot than last year's model, and a high price.

reviews.creator: Padel MaDs
reviews.quote: è una racchetta che davanti non spinge
reviews.summary: Tests the racket at 358 g without overgrip, with 3K carbon and a multilayer rubber that feels medium tending to hard. Finds the back of the racket good: control is high and lobs come out well when the arm is used. Calls the sweet spot centred but not big, with the blade feeling a little hollow at the third hole. Finds it gives no help at the front and needs a lot of arm, though more offensive than last year's model. Rates the four shock absorbers and the Vibra Drive as useless. Praises the open bridge for handling, but doubts the technologies matter when the materials are cheap and the paint wears quickly.
reviews.more: Compares it with last year's model, which was not offensive at all, and finds this one a bit more so. Notes the racket is the model of a pro player, whose own version is likely set up heavier with a harder rubber. Prefers the Ionic line among Bullpadel rackets. Warns that Bullpadel paint tends to scratch and chip because of the grooves. Announces the next video will cover the Vertex Geo.
highlights: sweet spot centred but not big

reviews.stood: Good control and easy lobs, plus an open bridge that helps handling.
reviews.trade: Gives no help at the front and needs a lot of arm.

reviews.creator: el4Set
reviews.quote: es la pala con más control que yo recuerde que haya probado
reviews.summary: Compares the Neuron Edge with the Explo and the Hack on court after removing the heavy undergrip and fitting two overgrips. Measures 350 g and a 26 cm balance, calling it very light, and finds it has the least ball output and the hardest feel of the three. Rates it the winner in defence by a wide margin, with the most control they remember testing and very manoeuvrable. Finds volleys, bandeja and vibora agile but hard to accelerate. Calls smash performance weak for finishing points. Suits players who want maximum control and win by organising the point, not by power.
reviews.more: Notes a new diamond mould with a triangular frame, 3K carbon and a soft, hard, soft Multieva core, the only Bullpadel using that layout. Lists a 13 cm grip. Finds the surface roughness weak on all three rackets. Says the undergrip adds 15 g and is uncomfortable, so removes it. Prefers the Hack for aggressive play and sees the Explo as a middle option between power and control.
highlights: winner in defence by a wide margin
the most control they remember testing

reviews.trade: Little ball output and weak smashes, so it will not suit aggressive players.

reviews.creator: The Padel School
reviews.quote: there's a nice bit of pop to that immediately
reviews.summary: Compares the Neuron 02 Edge with the standard Neuron 02 on court from the back and at the net. Finds the geo shape gives a bigger surface area, slightly more head weight and a good medium balance. Feels more spring and rebound off the face, with a nice bit of pop that helps volleys and overheads. Notes good precision and a similar feel and maneuverability to the standard model. Says it suits a player who wants extra pop on aggressive shots without losing accuracy. Mentions the Neuron core, Prism Lock and vibration dampening are shared by both rackets, with the geo surface the main difference.
reviews.more: Compares it with the standard Neuron 02, which has 3k carbon, a medium balance and slightly more power than last year. Finds the standard model gives great control and accuracy from the back and at the net, but needs a harder hit to get power. Says the Edge can also work for aggressive players, since it keeps the feel and control while adding more power. Notes both rackets use the same Neuron core and Prism Lock design.

reviews.keyPoint: More power and pop than the standard 02.
reviews.stood: More spring and pop than the standard 02, with the accuracy kept.
reviews.trade: Slightly more head heavy than the standard Neuron 02.

reviews.creator: Setup Padel | Mario Pazos
reviews.quote: es una pala que funciona muy muy bien por arriba
reviews.summary: Tests it from the right side of the court despite normally playing the left, covering defence, volleys and overhead shots. Measures 363 g as tested and a balance of 25.5. Finds the dry, medium-hard feel gives control from the back of the court and lets them hit the bandeja, vibora and smash hard without sending balls long. Finds the volley is not its strongest area, though puts that down to their own technique. Notes a slightly smaller sweet spot than the Vertex 05 Geo. Recommends it to aggressive right-side players, and to defensive players who like a dry, firm feel. Rates it very highly.
reviews.more: Plays the whole test on the right despite being a left-side player, and says it made them rethink switching sides. Calls it the best of the 2026 Bullpadel range they have tried so far. Advises against adding weight because the glue damages the racket. Finds the 3K carbon has more effect here than on the Vertex 05 Geo and the 3D rough surface more useful than on sister rackets. Notes little vibration and good reactivity thanks to the air openings in the bridge.

volley is not its strongest area

reviews.trade: Volley feels less sharp and the sweet spot is slightly small.

reviews.creator: Tino
reviews.quote: The serves are powerful with this.
reviews.summary: Tries the red Fire edition after earlier renting the 2022 Electra Pro, playing on the right side. Finds the power very strong, rates hardness at 8/10 and calls it great for serving and returning fast backhand balls. Struggles with control and volleys, because a slight flick sends the ball back with a strong rebound. Notes the 12K carbon, teardrop shape, rough sand surface for spin and the comfortable stock strap. Finds the 12K Nox more balanced, while this one gives more power and needs adapting. Concludes it suits left-handed players who want to attack and smash, and says the red finish looks premium.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 12K Nox, finding that one good for both attack and defense, while the Siux gives more power and less control. Explains 3K as control oriented and 18K as hard power, with 12K in the middle. Expects to feel comfortable after two or three matches. Notes the 2027 lines are out, so 2026 rackets have dropped in price, and recommends the red version over the plain black one.

reviews.keyPoint: Powerful teardrop racket best suited to left-handed attackers.
reviews.stood: Very strong power, especially on serves and fast returns, with a stylish red finish.
reviews.trade: Harder to control and volley, better suited to left-handed players than right-side players.

reviews.creator: Canary Padel
reviews.summary: Tests the diamond shaped 12K carbon racket in defense, volleys, bandeja, víbora and smash, with live court footage for each. Finds very good ball output without losing control, a comfortable feel and a rough sandy surface that grips spin very well. Notes a medium to medium-high balance and long grip that make handling a little harder in defense, and a sweet spot that is not big. Rates the volley as its best zone, with bandeja and víbora second and smash good but not its strength. Calls it one of the most balanced rackets tested this year, suited to a wide audience.
reviews.more: Compares the smash feel with the Adidas Metalbone and Head Speed Pro, saying it is not in that power class. Describes the carbon as medium to medium-hard, with a medium hardness EVA core and a comfortable touch. Notes a longer than standard grip and a sandy texture expected to wear off over time but last longer than a normal one. Thinks it could suit both right-hand and left-hand players. Gives defense 6.5 to 7 out of 10.
highlights: one of the most balanced rackets

reviews.keyPoint: Balanced all-round racket that is best at the net.
reviews.stood: Very good ball output with control, plus a rough surface that grips spin.
reviews.trade: Sweet spot is not big and handling is harder in defense.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.summary: Tests a red-finish unit of the 2026 Electra Pro on the court at medium and high pace, from the back, at the net and in the air game. Finds the feel just under medium-hard, softer than the 2025, and more reactive. Rates the sweet spot as good and easy to find, with very good maneuverability at 263 mm balance. Notes less control and linearity when accelerating volleys, blocks and the flat smash. Likes the bandeja and the rulo to the fence. Calls it a step above the 2025 from the back and one of the most versatile rackets of 2026. Warns that other units may feel harder.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Pegasus Pro 2026, finding a very similar feel but more reactive, with possibly a bit more power and a bit less control on volleys. Places it a notch softer than a 2025 AT10 12K. Notes the sandy rough finish feels slightly less marked than on the 2025. Cannot say whether units in the black or shadow finish feel drier, and asks players to share how theirs feels, since some reported a harder feel than the ST4.
highlights: sweet spot as good and easy to find
one of the most versatile rackets of 2026

reviews.stood: Easy sweet spot, comfort and very agile from the back of the court.
reviews.trade: Less linear and controllable when accelerating volleys and smashes at high pace.
reviews.compared: Siux Pegasus Pro 2026, Siux Electra Pro 2025, Nox AT10 12K

reviews.creator: Trypadel
reviews.quote: Elle offre un contrôle de balle optimal
reviews.summary: Tests the new ST5 on court and finds it very hard at impact yet very light. Calls it a good control racket in defence with no need to hit the centre of the face to play the ball. Notes that it feels hard and the ball can be sent. Likes the sliced volley and rates the overhead as very clean with power still there. Describes ball control as optimal and the racket as very versatile. Recommends it for players who want to do everything, a compromise between tolerance, control, attack and defence.

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: el rugoso arenoso es de los mejores del mercado
reviews.summary: Tests the hybrid shaped 12K carbon racket on court at 356 g and 26.5 cm balance, measured with an overgrip. Finds maneuverability very good, with a sweet spot just below a diamond racket and a dry, almost medium hard feel. Notes that the dry touch makes players push the ball to gain speed, and hitting high on the face makes the ball lose some speed. Rates the sandy rough surface among the best on the market. Calls it a balanced racket with no strong or weak point, best for players who use the vibora more than the smash.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Nox AT10 18K, which is softer with a bigger sweet spot and more explosive on the smash. Finds the Bullpadel Neuron 02 slightly stiffer. Notes the balance is higher than the AT10, which helps volleys feel lively and light. Points out that the red and black versions play the same and only the paint differs. Suggests it for summer, when a less reactive racket keeps control.
highlights: sandy rough surface among the best

reviews.keyPoint: Balanced hybrid with a dry touch and no weak point.
reviews.stood: Very good maneuverability and one of the best sandy rough surfaces.
reviews.trade: Sweet spot is localized and high hits lose speed, so smashing is not its strength.
reviews.compared: Nox AT10 18K, Nox AT10 12K, Bullpadel Neuron 02

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: A racket that gave me confidence
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 ST5 Pro on court at an actual weight of 355 g with a 27 cm balance, and calls it probably the ST version liked most so far. Calls it a complete hybrid with medium sweet spot, generous ball output and excellent spin, more communicative and less nervous than the 2025 model. Finds it easy to use at the net and from the back, with a firm feel that does not tire the arm. Notes the tip gets stiff, so players hitting there are not served well. Rates it 8 for power and ball output, 9 for spin, and recommends it for intermediate players and up.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Siux Phenix and Pegasus, finding it less explosive than the Phenix and a bit less maneuverable than both. Sees the Counter Viper 2026 as close, with slightly more explosiveness, while this one moves better. Advises subtracting 10 g from the weight printed on the handle, since Siux weights include strap and packaging. Suggests buying a second wrist strap for summer. Finds the sanded face held up well on a used test racket.
highlights: firm feel that does not tire the arm

reviews.creator: Padel Review
reviews.quote: ad alti ritmi ti permette un grande controllo di gioco
reviews.summary: Tests the Electra Pro ST5 2026 from the baseline, at the net and on overhead shots, then plays a points game. Finds a drier racket with a smaller sweet spot than last year, closer to the ST3 than the ST4. Calls it very manoeuvrable at 358 g with medium balance, and finds good control at high pace. Says balls come up short at slow pace and it is not a cannon. Rates control 7.5, spin 8, sweet spot 6.5. Suits technical left-side players who want a fast rhythm.
reviews.more: Notes a teardrop shape, 12K carbon faces, hard EVA rubber and a rough sanded surface. Finds less ball exit than last year, so players need to aim for depth. Says the flat smash has little inertia, while the por tres and rulo work better, though the rulo to the fence is rarer than on the previous model. Advises two hands on blocks because the grip is a little small. Rates the por tres and vibora 8.

balls come up short at slow pace

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: Se non la colpisci bene, la palla non esce.
reviews.summary: Tests it over three matches, starting on the right side and then moving left, and adds a session with a left-side friend. Finds a smaller sweet spot, a heavier feel and poor output off centre, so the ball does not come out when not hit cleanly. Feels power when pushing and finds vibrations well managed. Calls spin only good, below earlier Electra models. Says control exists only inside the sweet spot. Sees it as suited only to very clean, technical players and not to defensive ones. Would not buy it, as more complete and easier rackets exist.
reviews.more: Warns of three buying mistakes: assuming it is the natural evolution of earlier Electra models, testing it too little, and overrating how clean the hitting is. Finds lobs hard to lift from the right side. Notes a left-side friend had similar problems with off-centre hits and low feel. Says it is the first racket in the format they would put in the bin, not because it is unusable but because it is too limiting.
highlights: control exists only inside the sweet spot

reviews.keyPoint: Demanding racket that punishes any off-centre hit.
reviews.stood: Power is present when pushing and vibrations are well managed.
reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot and little help for defensive or right-side players.

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.quote: tengo una pala bastante más controlable con esta dureza un poquito más alta
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Electra Pro at 362 g with the original grip, balance around 26.8 cm, across defence, mid court, volley and smash. Finds a harder, more technical racket than last year's ST4 Pro, with a smaller sweet spot and less ball exit at medium and slow pace. Rates control better at faster rhythm and power higher, mainly on flat smashes and the smash for three. Notes that off-centre hits and forced shots come out shorter, and blocks need more effort. Calls handling very similar to last year. Recommends a medium weight of 360 to 365 g over a heavier one, since the high balance can handle slightly worse.
reviews.more: Places it close to the Pegasus Pro in hardness, with more power thanks to extra rebound. Compares it to the ST3, and says players who liked that racket may like this more, since it adds a little rebound while keeping control. Ranks the court zones where it felt best as víbora and bandeja, smash, volley, then defence. Notes the change aims at players who found last year's version too bouncy.
highlights: flat smashes and the smash for three
reviews.short: Tests the 2026 Electra Pro at 362 g with the original grip, balance around 26.8 cm, across defence, mid court, volley and smash. reviews.keyPoint: More technical and attacking than last year's version.
reviews.stood: Better control at fast pace and more smash power than the ST4.
reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot and shorter balls on off-centre hits or forced shots.
reviews.compared: Siux Electra ST4 Pro, Siux Electra ST3, Siux Pegasus Pro, Siux Fenix

reviews.creator: OngoalSweden
reviews.quote: Finns mycket bra grejer i det här racket.
reviews.summary: Tests the Electra in a group session of the 2026 Siux range, hitting rallies, overheads and volleys on court. Finds it gives more help and speed than the Diablo, with real feeling for the ball. Notes that the sandpaper surface gives spin for rolled shots, and that power is there when going for a flat hit. Likes the extra snap on overheads and volleys. Hears the brand expert say it is now 12K instead of 15K last year, lighter, solid at the back on blocks and volleys, and more capable when adding speed. Calls it offensive but suited to many players, from power hitters to those wanting feel and angles.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Diablo, which demands more swing and gives less free speed. Says the Diablo suits players who follow through and feel the ball all the way. Finds the Electra easier for a player who uses a lot of wrist and has less follow through. Encourages players to try several models if they get the chance, since more testing makes it easier to know which one feels best.
reviews.short: Tests the Electra in a group session of the 2026 Siux range, hitting rallies, overheads and volleys on court. reviews.keyPoint: Offensive racket with spin and feel for many players.
reviews.stood: More help and speed than the Diablo, with spin from the sandpaper surface.

reviews.creator: Otro Nivel Padel
reviews.quote: The maneuverability improved and the power improved.
reviews.summary: Tests the racket on court against the Valkiria Pro, hitting from the back, at the net and on smashes. Finds it much harder than the Valkiria, with less control from the back but slightly easier to maneuver. Calls it hard yet very easy to maneuver, easier than last year, with a lot of power, also more than last year. Rates the sweet spot as medium and not that big. Likes the direct touch at the net and finds smashes very easy. Rates it 9.7 out of 10 and calls it a racket for pro level offensive players who finish points, not for builders.
reviews.more: Gives the Valkiria Pro the same 9.7 out of 10 but calls that one a hybrid racket that suits everybody. Places the Valkiria Pro closest to the Diablo Pro, with a slightly softer touch. Finds the Electra harder than last year, and says power and maneuverability both improved. Notes that giving pressure feels much nicer with it and that smashes feel really nice. Recalls saying in another review that it was softer than last year, but now finds it harder.
reviews.short: Tests the racket on court against the Valkiria Pro, hitting from the back, at the net and on smashes. Finds it much harder than the Valkiria, with less control from the back but slightly easier to maneuver. Likes the direct touch at the net and finds smashes very easy. Rates it 9.7 out of 10 and calls it a racket for pro level offensive players who finish points, not for builders.
reviews.keyPoint: Hard, powerful finisher racket for pro offensive players.
reviews.stood: Big power and easy smashes while staying easy to maneuver.
reviews.trade: Medium sweet spot, and not for builders or defensive players.

reviews.creator: Gera Padel
reviews.quote: es una de las mejores opciones que tenemos en el mercado
reviews.summary: Describes the 2026 Electra Pro, Franco Stupaczuk's racket, as a black and red teardrop shape with a dry feel and a medium to medium hard firmness. Finds the dry feel helps a lot with a control game, but says it asks for longer swings through the ball. Calls it one of the best options on the market for a versatile racket that does not punish much, since it is not too difficult to use. Rates it a good choice for players who want comfort with a bit of aggression and attack. Recommends it for aggressive right side players, or for left side players who want more control.
highlights: helps a lot with a control game
a bit of aggression and attack

reviews.trade: Asks for longer swings through the ball to get the best from it.

reviews.creator: Mohamed Nasser || Coach Mohsen
reviews.summary: Uses it at the back of the court and finds the control very good, placing the ball exactly where wanted. Rates the spin and slice as respectable, and lobs gave no problem. Gets an unreal amount of slice and effect on the volley. Finds all aerial shots good, with the rulo coming out especially strong. Calls blocks more stable than on the Leo, with no need to grip hard. Notes the Leo gives somewhat higher smashes and more power overall, a gap that body work can narrow. Feels it slightly heavier than the Leo, only because the Leo is very light. Lists a teardrop shape, 12K carbon and the sweet spot in the middle.
reviews.more: Compares it directly with the Leo, which they call the best racket for power in 2026. Sees the Electra Pro as the steadier choice on blocks, while the Leo wins on smash height. Stresses that it still counts as very light, so nobody should expect a heavy racket after switching from the Leo. Lists the weight range as 355 to 375 and the brand hardness mark as 08. Suggests the best contact point sits in the middle of the face.
highlights: Rates the spin and slice as respectable
unreal amount of slice and effect
the rulo coming out especially strong

reviews.stood: Very good control from the back of the court and heavy slice on volleys.
reviews.trade: Less smash height and overall power than the Siux Leo.

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: mi fa giocare veramente con un comfort pazzesco
reviews.summary: Tests the Electra Pro in the Shadow finish on court, scoring each shot out of 10. Finds the sweet spot wide, rounded and starting low on the face, and gives 10 for the basic shot, low wall exit, block and smash. Gives 9 for high shots and high wall exit because it does not reach maximum power, though it cuts very well. Rates the feel medium hard, leaning to hard, at about 6.6. Calls it a versatile racket with extra power and cut. Says it should start cheaper, and notes shops already sell it for less.
reviews.more: Compares the sweet spot to the Babolat Viper Counter. Says the smash is slightly behind the Siux Phenix Pro, which has a little more. Thinks it may surpass the Viper Counter and similar rackets in the versatile segment. Notes an EVA core, 12K carbon faces with a sanded finish, neutral balance and a smart strap finish that matches the paint. Mentions a Red Fire version that only changes the colour and keeps the same internal build.
reviews.short: Tests the Electra Pro in the Shadow finish on court, scoring each shot out of 10. Finds the sweet spot wide, rounded and starting low on the face, and gives 10 for the basic shot, low wall exit, block and smash. Calls it a versatile racket with extra power and cut. Says it should start cheaper, and notes shops already sell it for less.
reviews.keyPoint: Versatile racket with extra power, cut and a wide sweet spot.
reviews.stood: Wide sweet spot and a block with very comfortable feel.
reviews.trade: Does not reach maximum power on high shots, and the launch price is high.
reviews.compared: Babolat Viper Counter, Siux Phenix Pro

reviews.creator: KB Sports Clips
reviews.quote: this is a great tunable attacking racket for good players
reviews.summary: Goes through the diamond shaped, head heavy racket at 38 mm thick, with a base weight of 345 to 360 g and removable weights up to 11.2 g that can be moved for power or control. Describes a 16K carbon aluminized face as stiff and fast but less harsh than the harder carbon, over a soft EVA core. Finds the sweet spot high and compact, calls smashes great, and says blocks and low defense balls ask more of the player. Rates it a great tunable attacking racket for good players. Says beginners, defensive players and anyone with elbow or wrist trouble should look elsewhere, and the cheaper team model suits players still building a smash.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Metalbone Team, which has a fiberglass face, no weight system and a heavier 360 to 375 g build, and is softer and more forgiving. Says the extra cost is worth it for players who actually tune the weights and swing fast enough for the stiffer face. Notes the harder version has a hard density core and feels drier, while the standard one has a bigger sweet spot and more trampoline feel. Points to a round, even balance model for right side players.
highlights: stiff and fast but less harsh
great tunable attacking racket for good players

reviews.keyPoint: Tunable diamond attacker for advanced players who smash.
reviews.stood: Movable weights let players tune power or control.
reviews.trade: Demanding head heavy racket, not for beginners or players with elbow trouble.

reviews.creator: Padel Smash TV
reviews.quote: I feel like I can do anything with this racket.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Metalbone on court in an open box and review with a second player. Calls it a favourite and in their top five rackets, well balanced, with good control in defence and at the net, and great power and overheads. Feels able to do anything with it. Rates it as the easier option compared with the HRD Plus, which is more difficult to control, and suggests it to players who are not yet pros. Gets agreement from the second player, who calls it the best of both worlds, with control and pop, and easy to use.
reviews.more: Places it in the middle of the Adidas line, between the HRD and the control version. Finds that many players pick up the HRD Plus, struggle to control it, and move to this one, which is more balanced. Thinks players can work up to the HRD Plus after using this one. Says it keeps the power and the defence while being easier to handle.
highlights: easier option compared with the HRD Plus

reviews.stood: Power and defence together in a well balanced, easy to use racket.

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: Every time you hit, you get the feeling of a full hit
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Metalbone 3.5 against the Metalbone Hard, which shares the mold and 16K carbon but uses a softer Soft Performance rubber. Finds it very reactive, with a considerably large sweet spot and a full, deep sound, though the ball can come out helplessly for players used to drier rackets. Weighs the standard unit at 366g with 27cm balance, and calls handling limited because of the long handle and the balance. Rates it easier than the Hard for smashes and baseline play, especially for players with modest arm speed. Prefers the Hard for control, but says removing the screws would make the 3.5 more agile.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Vertex, finding the 3.5 more reactive at similar hardness and less manageable. Estimates its sweet spot is about 15% larger than the Hard's. Notes that bandeja depth comes easily but the ball can fly into the glass, and that blocks bounce more than with the Hard. Points out that the 2026 version changes only the paint and a new slide safety rope.

reviews.keyPoint: Easy reactive power with a big sweet spot, limited handling.
reviews.stood: Very reactive, easy power and a large, forgiving sweet spot.
reviews.trade: Long handle and balance limit handling, and the ball can fly into the glass.
reviews.compared: Adidas Metalbone Hard, Bullpadel Vertex, Babolat Viper, Head Coello Pro

reviews.creator: PADELREVIEW ENG
reviews.quote: This racket is an absolute hammer.
reviews.summary: Reviews the 2026 Metalbone as a medium hard, diamond shaped attacking racket, with weight from 345 to 360 g and a high balance of 27.5 cm. Finds it similar to last year, with a slightly larger sweet spot and more ball output than the HRD version. Reports no arm discomfort despite the stiff feel. Rates baseline play as a pleasant surprise, volleys as stable and precise, and spin as a major strength. Calls overheads one of the strongest areas, with tremendous power from flat and kick smashes. Says it suits upper intermediate and advanced players, and weaker technique may struggle with the high balance.
reviews.more: Notes one of the biggest updates is a new wrist strap system. Lists carbon 16K, an EVA soft performance core, a rough surface and a longer handle. Finds the racket user friendly at moderate speed, with lobs, defensive shots and transitions feeling natural without forcing the swing. Says the extra ball output makes depth easier in medium pace rallies. Compared with the HRD version, rates it slightly easier to use, though it still needs good technique because of the high balance.

reviews.keyPoint: Versatile attacking racket with a huge overhead game.
reviews.stood: Overheads with tremendous power, plus surprisingly good baseline play and no arm discomfort.
reviews.trade: High balance demands good technique, so weaker players may struggle.

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: Ci vado in guerra 7 giorni su sette.
reviews.summary: Tests it over three matches, playing right side first and then left. Finds it a little harder and drier than earlier Metalbone versions, with the sweet spot good and maybe improved and ball output still interesting. Rates it best on the left side for attacking players who build points, with better control from the extra stiffness and a good push on smashes. Notes the new normal wrist cord still annoys at the side attachment and the grip feels slightly slippery. Warns players with sensitive elbows to avoid it. Sees little change from the 3.4 and advises buying that cheaper one instead.
reviews.more: Notes the 3.4 is much cheaper. Calls the 3.4 a no brainer unless budget is no concern. Suits intense, physical players who want to push hard, more from the left than the right. Includes the Adidas bag, weights, screwdrivers and an ergonomic head protector. Takes it onto court every day despite the price.
highlights: better control from the extra stiffness
sweet spot good and maybe improved

reviews.keyPoint: Strong left side attacker but costly next to the 3.4.
reviews.stood: Strong attacking feel and good sweet spot, especially played on the left side.
reviews.trade: Costly and may tire sensitive elbows.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: Pour la métal bon, c'est hyper facile.
reviews.summary: Tests the standard Metalbone with lab figures and on-court play, with the weights placed in the heart of the frame. Measures 356.4 g without the extra weights, with a 277 mm balance and a very high swing weight of 175.2, so power is high but maneuverability drops. Finds it nervous and fast, with little vibration for this power level, but demanding and tiring at the net because of the head-heavy balance. Notes the soft foam lets the ball leave the racket easily, which costs some control on volleys. Calls smashes very easy, even flat with a short swing. Suits advanced players with good technique who want power and some comfort.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Metalbone HRD+, which weighs 369 g, is stiffer and less forgiving, and is not advised for players with arm pain. Rates the standard model as the more polyvalent and more forgiving of the two, with scores of 72 for comfort, 71 for tolerance, 82 for ball output and 87 for power. Finds it adds ball speed without adding stiffness. Says it is not the best for soft defensive play, and that volleys need good timing.
highlights: little vibration for this power level
demanding and tiring at the net
even flat with a short swing

reviews.stood: Little vibration for such a powerful racket, and very easy smashes.
reviews.trade: Tiring and demanding at the net, and not the best for soft defensive play.

reviews.creator: Fun Padel Shop
reviews.quote: Smashes feel heavier, volleys feels more solid
reviews.summary: Reviews the Adidas Metalbone 2026 Ale Galan as a diamond shaped, head heavy racket built for attacking play. Finds power the main strength, with smashes feeling heavier and volleys more solid. Likes the adjustable weight system, which changes the weight by up to about 11 g, and the textured surface and hole pattern for spin. Calls it solid, premium and durable, and comfortable on the arm. Notes the sweet spot is smaller, so timing matters and off centre hits are felt. Rates it for advanced or experienced intermediate players who like finishing points, not for beginners or slow defensive styles.
reviews.more: Notes the grip is slightly longer than usual, giving more leverage on smashes and overheads. Says adding weight to the head gives more power and heavier shots, while removing it makes the racket easier to move. Finds it not very forgiving when the ball comes low and fast or off the fence, and says it asks for decent technique. Mentions a price of 389.

reviews.stood: Strong power for smashes and overheads, plus an adjustable weight system.
reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot, not forgiving and demanding for beginners.

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: non sento nulla sul braccio, davvero davvero eccellente.
reviews.summary: Tests the diamond shaped racket shot by shot, scoring each one out of ten: 10 for the volley, 10 for the high shot, 9.5 for the basic shot, 10 for the low wall exit and 9.5 for the smash. Finds the comfort very good, with nothing felt in the arm, and a rounded sweet spot close to the HRD. Notes the long handle takes getting used to. Worries that aluminium plates could add vibration in hot weather. Finds the retail price too much, though shops sell it for less. Suits advanced intermediate players, and intermediate players can use it too.
reviews.more: Says the rubber is not last year's and seems the same as the white Pro EDT released six months ago, adding a little comfort on touch. Finds the HRD more powerful on the high wall exit, the smash and the block, where this one feels slightly too elastic. Suggests removing the small weights for a lighter, more manoeuvrable racket. Calls it versatile, with extra push that suits a wide audience.
highlights: scoring each one out of ten
rounded sweet spot close to the HRD

reviews.trade: Price is too high and the long handle needs getting used to.

reviews.creator: Otro Nivel Padel
reviews.quote: Overall, very very nice racket.
reviews.summary: Tests it in defense, at the net and on smashes next to the Control and Hard versions in the new Metalbone range. Finds the weight sits in the top, so the sweet spot is small to medium and it takes longer to get the racket going from defense, though the touch stays fantastic. Notes more power than the Control, but only for players who swing with the whole arm and not just the wrist. Rates it 8.9 out of 10 and recommends it to high intermediate and pro players who smash a lot. Puts the weight at 345 to 360 g.
reviews.more: Says the feel is not softer than a Babolat Viper or harder than a Nox. Finds the ball goes deep into the racket instead of bouncing off, and the touch at the net is close to the Control. Calls it head heavy, which makes wrist motion harder. Likes the full black design more than last year's white, red and black. Picks the Control for their own level, and suggests players who smash a lot choose the Metalbone or the Hard.
highlights: sweet spot is small to medium
takes longer to get the racket going

reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot and slower to maneuver from defense, not for wrist players.
reviews.compared: Adidas Metalbone Control, Adidas Metalbone Hard, Babolat Viper

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: è una racchetta fisicamente impegnativa
reviews.summary: Buys the racket and finds it about 99% identical to the 2025 3.4, with only looks and a looped strap changed. Measures 356 g without the 12 g of removable weights, with a balance around 27.6 to 27.7 cm. Finds plenty of ball exit and spin, a sincere touch and a very good volley, but a heavy swingweight that tires after a while. Calls the sweet spot medium high, not very high, and says control and progression are lacking. Rates it as too pricey for what it offers. Says it may suit players used to heavy rackets, and prefers the Metalbone Carbon.
reviews.more: Prefers the Metalbone Carbon, which costs less, has more control and a healthier balance. Finds the HRD+ more progressive, with no response delay. Calls the Siux Phoenix Pro 5 easier to carry, and the Nox AT Attack 18K similar but better moving with a larger sweet spot. Notes the first minutes feel great but the weight wears on players later, and the strap is too long.
highlights: plenty of ball exit and spin
too high for what it offers

Finds plenty of ball exit and spin, a sincere touch and a very good volley, but a heavy swingweight that tires after a while. Calls the sweet spot medium high, not very high, and says control and progression are lacking. Rates it as too pricey for what it offers. Says it may suit players used to heavy rackets, and prefers the Metalbone Carbon.

reviews.summary: Describes the 2026 normal Metalbone as a medium hardness racket with 16K aluminised carbon, a Soft Performance rubber and a lot of rebound. Finds it very versatile and helpful for getting power easily in the aerial game. Recommends it for players who want help with ball speed and depth, not players who already accelerate well, since rebound can make the ball hard to control. Measures balance at 26.7 cm without screws and 27 cm with them, so warns it is head heavy and physically demanding. Notes weight of 345 to 360 g without screws, plus 12 g with them. Feels very similar to last year, with a new look and cord as the main changes.
reviews.more: Places its balance above the Control, which sits lower. Says the Hard shares the same 26.7 cm balance without screws and a similar weight. Describes the 2026 Carbon as giving better control in attack than a standard Metalbone because it rebounds less. Mentions the 3D rough surface, a slightly longer handle, the same heart as last year and the Power Groove weight system on the frame.
highlights: help with ball speed and depth

reviews.quote: una pala muy potente de las más potentes que he probado sin duda
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Coello Pro against the 2025 version from the baseline, net, and overhead positions. Weighs the racket at 360 g with the factory grip removed and one overgrip, from a 370 g starting weight, with a high balance of 275 mm. Finds it 5 g lighter, with a more reactive rubber and a medium hard feel that gives good ball exit at medium speeds. Calls it one of the most powerful rackets tried, with a sweet spot above standard size. Notes some loss of control when blocking fast balls and a slightly demanding feel in long volley sessions. Suits players who want an attacking racket that helps from the back of the court.
reviews.more: Finds the 2026 more reactive, a bit easier to move, with an almost identical sweet spot and similar power at the net and in smashes. Notes the rough surface is slightly more marked, and the soft plug adds comfort. Rates the víbora a 10. Says power is less progressive in pure power than hard feel rackets. Suggests it suits less advanced players who want easy power, but feels demanding for those coming from a versatile racket.
highlights: one of the most powerful rackets tried

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: La potenza è nulla senza un po' di forza fisica
reviews.summary: Plays three matches, two on the right and one on the left, with the second version of the Coello signature. Finds it heavy and demanding, especially at the net, where quick close exchanges were usually lost, but says it behaves well from the back. Rates it as a very powerful attacking racket, though not as powerful as the Delta Pro, with spin only average. Says it gives its best on the left side for players who like to push and finish. Advises against it for baseline builders, players with shoulder or elbow trouble, and anyone without arm strength.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Delta Pro, which remains the most powerful racket tried so far, and with last season's first version, finding little difference in finishing. Notes it is 5 g lighter than the previous generation but does not feel the change clearly. Rates Head build quality as among the best, and says it becomes close to a best buy once the price drops. Suggests a classic left side hitter would put it in the bag, while an intermediate right side player might not.

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: c'est une machine à gagner le point
reviews.summary: Tests the Pro on court in defence, volleys, transition shots and smashes after measuring it at 361.1 g and 281 mm balance. Finds it a hammer: very head heavy, hard to control, and tiring, with a shoulder that felt it after 20 minutes. Rates comfort as very good, with no parasitic vibrations, and the 3D texture as strong for spin. Praises the kick smash and the ball speed once the timing is right. Cites scores of 96 out of 100 for raw power and 47 for manoeuvrability. Recommends it to offensive players with top technique and fitness, level 7 minimum.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Motion, which is lighter at 356.5 g with balance at 270 mm, easier to time and called the best compromise in the range for level 5 and up. Notes the Pro plays fast, a little like the Metalbone. Finds flat smashes harder and more tiring than kick smashes, though a well timed flat smash is exceptional. Warns that dropping the racket head on volleys opens the face and sends the ball out. Mentions the Team as the easiest of the three but with a trampoline effect.
highlights: the 3D texture as strong for spin

reviews.creator: the4Set — Pablo
reviews.quote: The Coello Pro is a physical racket because of its weight and high balance.
reviews.summary: Tests the new Coello Pro 2026 against last year's model, the Motion and the Extreme, with a ball output test, a hardness test and 10 smashes per racket in Madrid with used balls. Finds the weight down 5 g to 370 g with the same 27.2 cm balance, and a reactive feel that is not as hard and dry as expected. Notes a high but not small sweet spot and a solid feel on blocks. Warns that the high balance tires the arm faster than the Motion on víboras. Calls it one of the best power rackets for players with good technique and physical condition.
reviews.more: Finds the 5 g drop makes it easier to move than the 2025 version, with the víbora the shot where the difference showed most. Rates the Extreme Pro as drier, so more power has to come from the player. Notes the Motion is 10 g lighter with a 26.8 cm balance and suits players who are not in top physical shape. Mentions the soft butt cap replaces the sharp octagonal one. Describes Arturo Coello's own setup of 380 g, factory grip and one overgrip, with the protector removed.
highlights: high but not small sweet spot
one of the best power rackets

reviews.quote: Realmente uno de los sitios donde mejor se va a comportar esta pala.
reviews.summary: Tests it in defence, at the net and on smashes, with the original grip replaced by two overgrips, giving 369 g and a high balance of 27.2 cm. Finds a sweet spot larger than standard and a decent ball output for a medium hard racket. Calls it best in the vibora and bandeja zone and on smashes, where the high balance adds leverage and the ball runs with little effort. Struggles with handling in defence and on low volleys, where the ball often rises more than wanted. Recommends it for a backhand player wanting extra attacking help, ideally in a lighter weight.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 version: adds a replaceable wrist cord and a soft cap for vibration, drops 5 g of average weight and changes the rough texture pattern slightly, while feeling very similar at equal weight. Finds a ball output similar in style to the Adidas Metalbone Hard, with less rebound and more control. Points to the Coello Motion as better for defence and volleys, with less weight and balance.

Finds the flat smash easier than the por tres, because the head heavy balance makes it hard to turn the racket over. Rates the block volley as very good, with depth even on late contact. Warns that the high ball exit can send shots long when swinging hard.

reviews.creator: Padel Racket Australia
reviews.quote: On volleys, you get a really solid response.
reviews.summary: Describes the Xplo 2026 as firm and direct, with a really solid response on volleys. Finds that clean contact makes it easy to play a fast, deep ball and put opponents under pressure. Notes the geometric shape, 12K carbon face, multi Eva core and 3D grain rough finish for extra grip on the ball. Calls it more demanding off the back wall, because the higher balance and firmer feel mean preparing early and getting behind the ball. Finds it stable and controlled from the baseline when blocking faster balls. Says it suits advanced or strong intermediate players with good technique and that late or off-center contact is punished.

reviews.creator: Julien Seurin
reviews.quote: je crois que c'est mon top 1
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Xplo, a geometric diamond shape in 12K carbon with medium stiffness, against the Hack 04 and Vertex Geo through defence, volleys, smashes and match points with a sparring partner. Adds 14 g of lead in the head to reach 388 g, adds two overgrips and keeps the antivibration dampers. Finds it a balanced in-between on rigidity, more tolerant than the Hack but less than the Vertex Geo. Notes less vibration on off-centre hits than last year, which they suspect comes from the added lead. Likes it overhead and in volleys, and calls this setup their top 1 for now.
reviews.more: Compares it with two other Bullpadel rackets. Finds the Vertex Geo softest and most forgiving but short on control when hitting hard, so ranks it third. Finds the Hack 04 stiffest, with a strong hitting feel but little room for error when off-centre. Puts the Xplo in the middle on volleys and second on waiting smashes, and sees little gap with the Hack. Admits being more used to the Xplo may bias the result, and says a switch in March is possible.

reviews.creator: Otro Nivel / Justpadel — shared test
reviews.quote: I like this a lot with the volley.
reviews.summary: Tests the normal 12K carbon Xplos against the softer Xplos Comfort on a cold Dutch court, covering defence, volleys, smashes and viboras. Finds the shape gives a very big sweet spot, about 70% of the racket, though the ball needs to be hit high on the racket for power. Rates power at six or seven out of 10 and notes a lot of spin. Calls it the best Bullpadel racket at the net for volleys. Finds it heavy at 365 to 375 g, with the weight felt in the follow through. Rates it 8.5 out of 10 for pro level players only.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Xplos Comfort, which uses softer Fibrix, and finds the Comfort a bit too soft at the back, possibly because of the cold, rating the Comfort 8.0 out of 10 for intermediates. Prefers the normal Xplos from the back and at the net. Suggests a Hack Hybrid or Vertex Hybrid for players who struggle with balls off the glass, as those are easier to maneuver. Would ask for 365 g and removes the shock out to save about 4 g. Finds it too heavy for female players.

weight felt in the follow through

reviews.quote: It moves better than the hack, but worse than the Neon.
reviews.summary: Tests the Explo against the Neuron Edge and the Hack after removing the Esacore undergrip and fitting two overgrips. Measures 25.5 cm balance and 355 g without the Esacore, with 12K carbon and a 12.5 cm grip. Finds it sits in the middle of the three for control, power and maneuverability, with low ball output and a stiff, dry feel. Calls the sweet spot smaller than the Neuron Edge, so clean technique is needed at the net. Names the glossy, barely rough surface as the biggest downside because spin shots are harder. Does not find it more powerful than the Hack. Suits players wanting a middle ground between power and control.
reviews.more: Compares it with last season's Explo, which is cheaper than the new one, and suggests the older one makes more sense. Notes the new version adds dampeners to reduce vibration and ball output. Finds it moves better than the Hack but worse than the Neuron Edge. Reports it feels similar to the Neuron Edge at the net but is more reactive. Says the Hack wins on smashes, while the Neuron Edge is best for control.

reviews.creator: Padel5
reviews.quote: Los rulos a la reja son uno de sus puntos fuertes.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Xplo and finds it built for aggressive play without losing the control needed on court. Rates volleys as stable, firm and fairly precise, with good ball speed when well positioned, though its weight makes it slow to move when arriving forced with a loose arm. Calls rulos to the fence one of its strengths because the racket grips the ball. Says drop shots are not its best area, since the ball can end up high or long. Rates defence as decent for this type of racket, with good ball exit. Suits medium to high level players who want to dominate the net.
reviews.more: Notes bandejas come out with good depth without squeezing hard, which keeps opponents at the back, though softer short ones need good hands to avoid stopping mid court. Says drop shots have touch but the racket is not made for delicate play, and extra force leaves the ball high or long. Sums up the strengths as power without losing control, easy spin and strong play at the net. Lists weaker points as not being the lightest or most comfortable for drop shots or long defensive spells.

Calls it powerful, with a sweet spot in the centre and a different response in the upper area without holes. Finds it hard to control at the net when the ball comes in fast, but comfortable at low speed. Suspects the glossy paint and stiff 12K carbon clash with the medium soft multi EVA. Ranks it last for hardness among the 2026 Bullpadel rackets tried.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Neuron 02, which feels more solid and holds the ball better against hard shots, and which uses 3K carbon. Describes the Xplo as having a drum feel, similar to the Vertex but less solid. Does better on drop shots with the Xplo than with the Neuron. Orders hardness as Hack 04 2026, Neuron 02, Vertex, then Xplo. Notes both rackets use multi EVA rubber.

reviews.quote: Me gusta ese tactito seco que te da.
reviews.summary: Tests the 2026 Xplo on court, finding it very close to last year's model. Measures a balance of about 25.7 cm, below the stated figure, and a weight of 372 g with everything fitted. Likes the dry feel, good ball exit and a standard, slightly wider sweet spot, with no noticeable vibrations. Finds power only fair and doubts the claim that it is the brand's most powerful racket. Dislikes the light 3D rough texture and the glossy finish, which lets the ball slip. Rates the volley as the strongest part, while the smash is only average. Recommends it to right-side players who defend but want a little more bite.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Vertex Geo, finding the Xplo a touch less aggressive but more versatile, with a slightly wider sweet spot and easier defence. Puts the Hack as the brand's aggression reference, then the Geo, then the Xplo, then the standard Vertex. Notes the 12K face feels slightly harder than the Geo's 3K, and guesses higher carbon density and the gloss explain it. Would like a stiffer 3K version.

reviews.summary: Tests it from the baseline, at the net and on smashes, then scores most traits at 7.5. Finds the hard feel gives plenty of control when the pace goes up, and the ball stays in court even on aggressive forehands. Calls it very manoeuvrable, with excellent blocks on volleys. Dislikes the lack of spin, scored 6.5, and finds smashes quick but not powerful. Notes 354 g weight and 25.7 cm balance. Recommends it for aggressive right-side players with a good level and a strong arm, since soft shots land short.
reviews.more: Calls it more defensive than the Neuron 02 Edge, which they find more offensive and also fine on the left side. Would pick the Edge at the same price. Finds this third edition not very different from the first one, only harder. Says it is not an easy racket and rewards constant intensity.
