Says it suits players wanting a more offensive racket without going too hard.
reviews.keyPoint: Versatile attacking racket with a very wide sweet spot.
reviews.stood: Wide sweet spot, easy ball output and better handling than the Pro.
reviews.trade: High balance still demands care in handling and fast defensive play.
reviews.compared: Head Coello Pro, Fenix Elite, Adidas Metalbone, Bullpadel Neuron 02

reviews.creator: Otro Nivel Padel
reviews.quote: it's a very usable and a likable racket
reviews.summary: Tests the Motion alongside the Vibe, Team and Pro, playing the same shots with each from the back of the court, at the net and on smashes. Finds it sits in between hard and soft, with a clicking sound and a lot of control. Notes much more power than the Team without forcing the shot, and a better smash and vibora. Calls the sweet spot nice and the racket very easy to play with. Rates it 8.9 out of 10, and says beginners can stay with the Team and softer hitters can skip the Pro.
reviews.more: Compares it with the rest of the line: the Vibe feels harder and direct, the Team softer with a smaller sweet spot, and the Pro more direct and clunkier. Finds the step up from the Team noticeable on kick smashes and viboras, which justifies the extra money once rallies get quicker. Suspects the racket is not full 3K carbon, since the label says carbon hybrid HS, so it may not bounce the highest. Likes the crown design.
highlights: much more power than the Team
reviews.short: Tests the Motion alongside the Vibe, Team and Pro, playing the same shots with each from the back of the court, at the net and on smashes. Finds it sits in between hard and soft, with a clicking sound and a lot of control. Notes much more power than the Team without forcing the shot, and a better smash and vibora. Calls the sweet spot nice and the racket very easy to play with. Rates it 8.9 out of 10, and says beginners can stay with the Team and softer hitters can skip the Pro.
reviews.keyPoint: Balanced racket that suits most intermediate players well.
reviews.stood: Sits between power and control, and is easy to play with.
reviews.trade: Suspects it is not full carbon, so it may not bounce the highest.
reviews.compared: Head Coello Vibe, Head Coello Team, Head Coello Pro

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: Sembra abbia gli ammortizzatori questa palla perché è davvero comoda
reviews.summary: Tests it over three matches, merged into one account, and finds a softer Coello Pro with generous ball exit, very good vibration damping and no arm stress after two hard matches. Rates power as a step below the Pro, control good at medium pace but prone to going long when pushing hard, and maneuverability demanding at the net. Calls the build solid, in line with other Head rackets. Says it suits players who hit hard and want a sturdy racket, less so precision players. Puts it in the middle box, needing some muscle to handle.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Coello Pro, finding the Motion gives more elastic help in tough spots but does not feel different enough to justify a separate model. Warns that a full power viper can slip out of the hand and go long. Calls it well spent. Says Head prices below other top brands and sees it as not quite a best buy at the level of the Extreme Motion, but still well placed.
highlights: no arm stress after two hard matches
prone to going long when pushing hard
reviews.short: Tests it over three matches, merged into one account, and finds a softer Coello Pro with generous ball exit, very good vibration damping and no arm stress after two hard matches. Rates power as a step below the Pro, control good at medium pace but prone to going long when pushing hard, and maneuverability demanding at the net. Calls the build solid, in line with other Head rackets. Says it suits players who hit hard and want a sturdy racket, less so precision players. Puts it in the middle box, needing some muscle to handle.
reviews.keyPoint: Comfortable, solid racket that still needs some muscle.
reviews.stood: Vibration damping that spares the arm and a generous ball exit.
reviews.trade: Demanding to move at the net, needs some muscle.
reviews.compared: Head Coello Pro, Head Extreme Motion

reviews.creator: Xeexi1707
reviews.quote: es una pala que responde muy bien
reviews.summary: Tests it on court with a coach feeding balls, covering baseline, volleys, viper, bandeja and smash. Finds the feel medium hard but not dry, with a reactive rubber that gives good ball exit. Notes the high balance makes the racket hard to move at the net, though the 360 g weight keeps it fairly manageable. Calls it great for accelerating the ball and attacking from above. Says smashes are the strength for players who can finish, while their own game is less aggressive. Rates it as an attacking racket that holds up in defence thanks to its lower weight than the Pro, suited to players who want power without losing control.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 Motion and finds almost no difference in rubber, balance or setup. Notes small changes in the end cap, an easier string swap and a bronze and garnet look instead of black and red. Says the 2025 version is enough for players who care about price rather than design. Compares it with the Pro, which weighs about 10 g more, and finds the Motion easier to handle in defence and at the net. Recommends both years.
highlights: reactive rubber that gives good ball exit
reviews.short: Tests it on court with a coach feeding balls, covering baseline, volleys, viper, bandeja and smash. Rates the sweet spot as larger than standard and the feel as medium plus a little. Finds power easy at the net but a bit short for players who want 100% power. Calls the 3D rough useful for grip but not very marked. Sees it as a versatile racket suited to intermediate players who want easy ball output.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2025 model, which feels similar but less manageable on the baseline. Places it at the level of the Stress Motion, only a little easier to move, and a bit more reactive than the Extreme Motion but softer. Notes the new soft cap with replaceable cord and a slightly more marked 3D rough. Misses a little more texture and points to Head strips as an option. Finds it forgiving in blocking volleys unless the hand is held very hard.
highlights: much more manageable than last year
sweet spot as larger than standard
short for players who want 100% power

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: c'est bien plus facile à jouer que la pro
reviews.summary: Tests the Motion on court against the Pro and Team versions, after lab measurements of 356.5 g, 270 mm balance and 63 RA. Finds it much more manageable than the Pro, with better timing and ball direction, though it stays head heavy and limited for chiquitas and short, slowed gestures. Calls it moderately tolerant on high balls, losing control and length when the hit is off centre. Rates the smash very powerful, with flat smashes easier than on the Pro. Cites ratings of 85 for power and 61 for maneuverability out of 100, and calls it the best compromise of the range. Recommends it to intermediate plus players, level 5 minimum, with good physical condition.
reviews.more: Notes the Motion keeps the Pro's hybrid carbon surface and 3D print texture, but drops about 6 g and one centimetre of balance. Finds it easier to bring arm speed on flat smashes. Adds that the Pro has a much higher inertia, 193.1 against 174.2 on the Motion. Warns that both Pro and Motion need very good physical condition, and on the Motion mostly in movement, to stay behind the ball and hit in front. Finds the Team more forgiving and comfortable but prone to rebound errors.
highlights: much more manageable than the Pro

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.quote: it's a racket that has become slightly more comfortable than previous versions
reviews.summary: Tests it first with the Hesacore and an overgrip at 380 g, then removes the Hesacore and adds two overgrips for 360 g and a balance of 26.7 cm, finding it easier to move. Rates handling as standard and finds a slightly larger sweet spot and more reactive feel than the previous Hack. Likes the confident control at a fast pace, though finds it less dry and a little less controlled than older versions. Notes it penalises hits outside the sweet spot and gives less ball speed than more reactive rackets. Recommends it for technical players who accelerate and want a racket that depends on them, not for those wanting attacking help.
reviews.more: Compares it with a Head Coello Pro, which is heavier and more head heavy, and says a Metalbone Hard gives far more ball output in the three point smash. Calls the flat smash better than before, but finds the three point smash hard to get value from. Warns that a heavy forearm feeling usually comes from weight, so removing the Hesacore and adding overgrips can help.
highlights: confident control at a fast pace
penalises hits outside the sweet spot

reviews.creator: Mohamed Nasser || Coach Mohsen
reviews.quote: المضرب ممتاز الهاك فور انصح بيه بشده عن الهاك 3
reviews.summary: Compares the Hack 04 2025 with the Hack 03 2024 on court, playing defensive and attacking shots, volleys and smashes. Finds the Hack 04 much lighter than last year's racket, though unsure if that is just this unit, with full control in all directions and very good defence. Rates it clearly better than the Hack 03 and says the ball feels better on contact. Notes the unit tested is missing two of the four orange weight circles, so a complete version may feel different. Explains the circles can be moved up for power, down for control, or removed for less weight. Recommends the Hack 04 strongly to Bullpadel fans choosing between the two.
reviews.more: Says the Hack 03 felt good in smashes, volleys and groundstrokes but has aged. Calls the Hack 03 light overall, not heavy for them. Mentions an earlier Hack 03 split in two when hit against a wall, possibly a factory fault. Adds that another Hack 04 they tried felt better in hand than this one, and expects a complete version to be a different racket, not comparable with the Hack 03.
highlights: much lighter than last year's racket

reviews.keyPoint: Clearly better than its predecessor, with better ball feel.
reviews.stood: Control in all directions and better ball feel than the Hack 03.
reviews.trade: Tested unit lacked two weight circles, so a full version may differ.

reviews.creator: Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel
reviews.quote: you get a great sense of control, especially regarding speed
reviews.summary: Tests the Hack 04 head to head against the Vertex 04 in mid-March, in cold and rainy weather. Weighs the unit at 369g with a 25.5 cm balance and finds the head balanced despite the diamond shape. Rates the sweet spot as average and says it takes effort to find, especially in defense and on lobs, after switching from an AT10 18K. Praises the great sense of control over speed once used to the hardness. Gives it the points on vipers, bandejas and smashes, and calls it the overall winner. Suggests removing the Hesacore grip because it feels uncomfortable and too thick.
reviews.more: Finds the Vertex 04 more manageable, 12g lighter, with a slightly larger sweet spot and more rebound at low speed. Notes the Hack is harder overall despite its 18K outer layer, thanks to the extra Tricarbon layers. Says the Hack is the better choice from mid-court forward, while the Vertex suits play from the back. Mentions the eight orange dampeners add 4 or 5g and can be removed, and that the Hack could suit summer heat.
highlights: Rates the sweet spot as average
great sense of control over speed

reviews.stood: Control over ball speed and extra raw power in smashes.
reviews.trade: Smaller sweet spot, harder to find in defense and on lobs.

reviews.creator: Peter Consuegra
reviews.quote: es una pala muy buena para iniciar un contragolpe
reviews.summary: Tests it on court after going through the brand specs, with a diamond shape, 18K tricarbon face and a weight of 365 to 375 g. Finds it improved on the model from two years ago in manoeuvrability, sweet spot and a little in control, but dry in feel and punishing off the sweet spot. Rates the viper outstanding and the bandeja very good, with fast volleys and quick counterattacks from the back. Finds it gives little control help at medium and low pace, so it does not suit lower intermediate players. Calls it an offensive racket for advanced players.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Vertex 04, played for the last two years, and finds the Hack clearly behind in control but ahead for hard hitting, short quick strokes and blocks. Feels more comfortable overall with the Vertex as the more versatile racket, and finds spin easier there. Notes removable dampeners that can be moved to change stiffness and a custom weight system for shifting balance. Says the Hack suits players who like a hard, dry feel.

reviews.stood: Fast, aggressive hitting, especially the viper, volleys and blocks.
reviews.trade: Little control help at slow pace and punishes off-centre hits.

reviews.creator: Probando Palas
reviews.summary: Tests the 2025 Paquito Navarro model at 370 g with a 262 mm balance, and finds it heavier and less manageable than older versions because of the four dampeners. Rates the sweet spot as quite good and wider thanks to the dampeners, with little vibration despite the medium hard touch. Finds it very reactive, so the ball leaves the blade fast at medium pace and some control is lost. Likes it more at high pace, especially on viper shots and finishing balls. Calls the 3D roughness not very marked, so spin is the weak point. Suits players who liked earlier Hack versions and want an attacking racket.
reviews.more: Welcomes the removed metal protector, which gives a cleaner blade and allows an adhesive protector. Finds the new circular hole pattern helps when blocking, whereas last year's version felt stuck on centred hits. Suggests removing the Gescor and a couple of dampeners to improve handling. Dislikes the cord leaving the side of the grip, which makes the grip shift when hooking the blade, and finds the standard grip too soft. Sees it as possibly one of the best rackets of 2025 after limited testing.
highlights: heavier and less manageable than older versions

reviews.stood: Reactive ball exit and good progression at high pace, especially on viper shots.
reviews.trade: Heavier and less manageable than older versions, with little spin from the roughness.

reviews.creator: Simone Mazzola Padel
reviews.quote: ha ancora il suo bel carattere e se serve sa chiudere con importante veemenza
reviews.summary: Tests the 2025 Hack on court and finds a clear change from earlier versions: less rigid and less aggressive, with softer touch and better ball exit. Rates power as still good but not comparable to older models, and finds control easier. Notes a sweet spot wider than before but not large, with a clear drop in performance off centre. Finds it demanding at the net and on repeated overhead shots, and dislikes the wrist strap exiting from one side of the handle, which curls up. Praises lobs and volleys. Suggests it for upper intermediate to advanced left side players with good fundamentals, not for lower levels.
reviews.more: Compares the strap problem with the Neuron, finding it more bothersome here. Calls the old Hack a rigid, aggressive left side racket and says this one keeps its character and can still close points with force. Finds it surprisingly good in defence and on lobs. Notes it does not vibrate but still causes some fatigue in longer matches.
highlights: softer touch and better ball exit

reviews.stood: Much better ball exit, helping defence and lobs, with more comfort.
reviews.trade: Demanding at the net and overhead, sweet spot not generous, and the strap curls up.

reviews.creator: Padel Review
reviews.summary: Tests it after removing the Hesacore and fitting two overgrips, giving 366 grams and a 27 cm balance, then plays from the baseline, at the net and with overheads. Finds it the best Hack tested so far: more controlled than the previous version, with a bigger sweet spot, yet still a bulky diamond racket that feels heavy and gets woody when the ball is hit off centre. Calls it an aggressive, technical attack racket that returns heavy balls and rewards players who hit with intent. Suggests it suits intermediate-high level players, mainly on the left side. Rates it as good value for a signed racket.
reviews.more: Reports that removing the Hesacore gave more handling and a higher balance, and says they will do it on every Bullpadel that ships with one. Notes the weight is felt at the net even at low speed, so suggests using the non-dominant hand to keep the racket high. Says the new rubbers soften vibrations, though the arm still tires on repeated overheads. Compares the bulk to the Vertex and says Tapia's Nox rackets are more powerful.

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: it's a racket that works very well
reviews.summary: Compares the 2025 Hack with last year's edition and finds a more mature racket with a denser touch, better ball output and clearly better spin, while the easy behaviour of the 2024 is kept. Rates sweet spot 7, control 8, spin 8.5, volleys 8.5 and smash with kick 8.5. Finds it a little drier and short of mass in the head, so the flat smash is only decent. Calls it a serious racket for players who can handle a medium small sweet spot, easier than older Hack models. Would have preferred it a bit more demanding.
reviews.more: Notes the specs run from 365 to 375 g with a high balance, plus a new channel around the frame and no metal shield. Gives 368 g and a balance of 25.5 and finds it moves well. Points out that the stock grip system weighs more than two overgrips, so weight comparisons with other brands need care. Mentions a CMF version that is easier and untested by them. Finds the vibora works well, with spin coming easily, and the smash with kick helpful.
highlights: short of mass in the head

reviews.stood: Spin and ball output improved, with a denser touch and easy handling.
reviews.trade: Less demanding than older Hack models and lacks some mass in the head.

reviews.creator: the4Set
reviews.quote: the Hack accelerates slower but reaches a higher speed
reviews.summary: Compares the Hack 04 2025 head to head with the Bullpadel Xplo on court, after removing the Hesacore grip. Weighs it at 364 grams with a 27 cm balance, and notes 18K carbon and Multieva foam. Finds the matte finish and extra holes give better ball grip and spin than the Xplo. Rates it better on volleys, with more weight on the ball and no power cap at high speed. Finds it harder to move and prepare than the Xplo. Calls power basically a tie after over 10 smashes each. Sees it suiting offensive players with good strength who want a high balance and dry feel.
reviews.more: Notes built-in vibration dampeners in four holes, which make the racket a bit stiffer. Mentions a 12 cm handle and a wrist strap placement that allows weight to be added to the handle. Points out that Bullpadel rates it 100 for power and 90 for control, the same as the Xplo. Finds the bandeja a tie, with the Hack adding more spin and weight but being harder to prepare. Prefers the Xplo personally for defense and ease of handling.
highlights: no power cap at high speed

reviews.stood: Matte face and extra holes give better spin, plus more weight on volleys.
reviews.trade: Harder to move and prepare than the Xplo, so less suited to defensive players.

reviews.quote: it's a lot softer and there's a bit more flex
reviews.summary: Tries the Hack 04 for the first time after a session hitting with it. Finds it a lot softer, with more flex, and says it absorbs the power more, so players have to give the shot a little more. Calls it a more advanced racket and points to a professional player who uses it. Rates the looks as a personal favourite. Describes the Hack 04 as a diamond shape that gives more power, with a round Hybrid version for control players. Says it suits an advanced player who already has power and perfected technique.

advanced player who already has power

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.quote: Sul resto dei colpi è davvero eccezionale.
reviews.summary: Weighs the racket on a scale and gets 369 g, matching the stated weight, with a 27 cm balance. Tests it on volleys, overheads, lobs, wall exits and blocks. Rates the volleys and high shots very highly, and calls it comfortable with no vibration on blocks. Finds good power and slice, though the impact feels strange at first. Finds the sweet spot placed high and not very wide, so lobs struggle when the ball is off centre. Says it suits intermediate advanced players up to professionals, and thinks the 2024 version had a wider sweet spot.
reviews.more: Compares it with the 2024 Hack 04, which had a slightly wider sweet spot, and says the new Tricarbon plates and multilayer Eva rubber change the racket completely. Notes that the power sits toward the top of the face, so hits need to land high rather than at the centre. Finds it very good for blocking and for wall exits under pressure, with basic shots easy and the ball staying low even with some topspin.
highlights: suits intermediate advanced players up to professionals

reviews.stood: Comfort, power and volleys, with no vibration on blocks.
reviews.trade: Sweet spot is high and not very wide, so lobs suffer off centre.

reviews.creator: Rodri Ovide
reviews.summary: Tests the Hack 04 after being a Vertex fan and ends up switching to it. Describes the concentric circular hole pattern, the surface roughness for spin, and the aerodynamic tube channel that the study says adds 10 to 15% more speed. Praises the Easy Vibe: on the four extremes it gives a more flexible sweet spot, closer to the center it gives a harder impact, and it cuts vibration by up to 49%. Feels very comfortable with the Hesacore grip system. Recommends it 100% and tells players in doubt to switch to the Hack.
reviews.more: Notes the Easy Vibe can be taken off and put back to change the balance of the racket. Adds that the Easy Vibe, the Tricor heart and the tube together make the racket built to reduce vibration and gain acceleration on impacts. Calls the speed gain a good improvement for players who want faster finishing and movement. Says they always chose the Vertex before and will now stay with the Hack for at least a trial period.

reviews.keyPoint: Easy Vibe tuning won over a longtime Vertex player.
reviews.stood: Adjustable Easy Vibe placement and reduced vibration.

reviews.creator: Padel Vlog Italia
reviews.quote: è la bella pro più giocabile, più immediata
reviews.summary: Answers viewer questions on the V3 after long testing, and gives an absolute yes to it. Finds the paint system improved and much more resistant after the problems of the V2 and V2.5. Notes 24K carbon, a balance of 27 cm and a bigger sweet spot, with more free power and clearly better maneuverability than earlier versions. Calls it the most playable and immediate Bela Pro, aimed at high level offensive players who bring arm and legs. Points to one drawback: a twist weight of 16.4 against 17.4 for rivals, so the racket recoils and shifts in the hands during fast exchanges at the net.
reviews.more: Places it in the family of big offensive rackets such as the Babolat Technical Viper, which reward good technique and a strong push. Says a modern offensive right side player can use it, but the level must be even higher. Finds it more explosive than the V2 and V2.5 and far more playable than the first version, with 165 inertia points that make it easy to play for its segment. Says the weight is no longer felt when moving around the court.
reviews.short: Answers viewer questions on the V3 after long testing, and gives an absolute yes to it. Finds the paint system improved and much more resistant after the problems of the V2 and V2.5. Notes 24K carbon, a balance of 27 cm and a bigger sweet spot, with more free power and clearly better maneuverability than earlier versions. Calls it the most playable and immediate Bela Pro, aimed at high level offensive players who bring arm and legs. Points to one drawback: a twist weight of 16.4 against 17.4 for rivals, so the racket recoils and shifts in the hands during fast exchanges at the net.
reviews.keyPoint: Most playable and explosive Bela Pro so far.
reviews.stood: Much more maneuverable and playable than earlier versions, with more free power.
reviews.trade: Lower twist weight gives more recoil and shifting in the hands at the net.
reviews.compared: Wilson Bela Pro V1, Wilson Bela Pro V2, Babolat Technical Viper

reviews.creator: Mejora Tu Padel
reviews.summary: Tests it on court with academy competition players alongside the softer Bela LS. Finds it a little harder than the LS but not much, with a very wide sweet spot, though the ball comes out less when pressed harder. Rates it very manageable and comfortable, and calls the sandy, aggressive texture very interesting. Describes the blade as very versatile, with the ball going where intended from the first moment. Suits players looking for an easy racket to use. Gives it five and a half to six for value. Would want a harder feel from the 24K carbon, a better cap and an interchangeable strap.
reviews.more: Prefers it a little over the Bela LS, which is softer and lighter with a low-density rubber. Notes that this year's Pro is much softer than earlier versions, so more players can use it, and that Bela plans to play this production model as standard rather than a customized one. Gives the LS a seven for value. Adds that value for the Pro improves if prices drop later.
highlights: five and a half to six for value

reviews.creator: Padel Review
reviews.quote: Buonissimo il punto dolce.
reviews.summary: Tests it on court with a second player across baseline, net and overhead play, then scores each shot. Finds the sweet spot wide and spin extreme, rated 9, thanks to the 3D sandblasted finish. Notes that the ball stays stuck on the face, so it suits fast rhythm and punishes slow play. Calls the ball exit controlled and not generous, and dislikes the drum like sound. Finds it very manoeuvrable at 366 g with mid balance. Says it is not a cannon but handles smashes and the vibora well. Sees it as a polyvalent racket for intermediate players and up. Prefers the older 2.5.
reviews.more: Lists changes against the 2.5: 24K carbon faces instead of 3K, Power Foam rubber and a bridge. Notes that blocks and flat lobs fall short unless pushed, and that cut lobs work better. Scores sweet spot 8, power 8 and value 6. Prefers the 2.5, which felt like a glove, with a touch and sound they liked more. Describes the touch as medium, almost soft.
highlights: sweet spot wide and spin extreme
suits fast rhythm and punishes slow play
ball exit controlled and not generous

reviews.creator: Fabio Ferro
reviews.quote: è una all round per davvero e fa tutto molto bene
reviews.summary: Tests the racket on the court from the baseline, volley, vibora, smash and kick smash, with constant comparisons to the Defy Pro. Finds a medium to medium-high sweet spot and a full, heavy ball exit that needs some pace to wake up, with immediate and easy spin. Calls it a true all round racket with good control, though the 370 g weight shows up over time. Notes the Defy Pro is more powerful and better when swinging harder, while this one is more generous. Says it suits a full intermediate or better who is used to heavy rackets, and not players wanting maximum power or a very manoeuvrable racket.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Defy Pro, Phenix Pro, Metalbone 3.4 and Velocity Pro, finding the Velocity Pro has more ball exit but less control. Suggests swapping the thick stock grip for a thinner one or overgrips to keep wrist fluidity. Points to the tubular frame as a quality sign that may help durability. Wonders whether the middle Bela V3 with Power Foam and a 3K face could be the best buy.
highlights: 370 g weight shows up over time

reviews.creator: the4Set
reviews.quote: But on defense, the V3 Pro feels much more comfortable than the V2.5
reviews.summary: Tests the Pro V3 in very hot conditions with the factory grip, which feels about the right size, and plans to swap it for two grips next time. Finds the sweet spot larger than on the V2.5, with defense much more comfortable and maneuverability similar despite 370 g and a 26.5 cm balance. Likes the new 3D sandy roughness most, which lets them feel the ball and place it. Rates it at 55% control and 45% power, with mixed feelings on smashes where more head weight would help. Calls it a mid to hard, versatile racket for players wanting a big sweet spot.
reviews.more: Notes the Pro uses 24K carbon for the first time, the plastic insert from the V2 and V2.5 is gone and the frame channels are reinforced. Says the standard V3 uses 3K carbon and weighs 5 g less, while the LS weighs 15 g less and adds comfort flex. Finds smash differences between the three barely noticeable. Prefers the V1 for its shorter grip length and dislikes the V2 handle system.
highlights: sweet spot larger than on the V2.5

reviews.creator: träna padel
reviews.quote: det här är för den toppavancerade spelaren
reviews.summary: Tests the Pro version of the Bela V3 family at 370 g with a 24K carbon overlay. Finds the rougher sandpaper surface, sharp hole technology and side stability channel give a better grip on the ball and a mild catapult effect. Rates it as stiffer than the other two variants, though a step back from the stiffest Wilson rackets before. Feels it still needs the player to do much of the work, yet it answers well when technique is there. Finds it light to move at the net despite the weight. Calls it a racket for top advanced players with a good arm release.
reviews.more: Compares it with the Pro V2.5, finding the new surface clearly rougher and the sides giving a catapult feel the older Bela line lacked. Describes the V3 at 365 g with a 3K overlay as softer and more forgiving, with the balance slightly closer to the hand. Describes the LS at 355 g as the lightest, with weight near the hand and plenty of help. Notes the Pro feels slightly more head heavy than the V3 but not extremely top heavy.
highlights: stiffer than the other two variants
light to move at the net

reviews.creator: Extreme Padel
reviews.quote: Elle a vraiment une superbe accroche.
reviews.summary: Tests it on court after lab measurements, finding 367.2 g and 263 mm balance against the brand's 370 g and 265 mm. Calls the grip on the ball incredible thanks to the 3D spin texture, which keeps the ball in the racket longer and adds precision. Finds smashes powerful, especially kicked ones. Notes a trampoline effect that sends lobs out fast, a restricted sweet spot that vibrates off centre, and only average handling, slightly better than the Wilson Defy. Recommends it to confirmed to expert players and advises against it for anyone with arm problems.
reviews.more: Compares the spin rating of 97 with 100 for the Wilson Defy, and does not feel the difference on court. Describes the Pro as versatile, with medium swing weight and medium stiffness. Presents the lighter Wilson Bela with 3K carbon, measured at 361 g, as more comfortable and forgiving but less powerful. Adds that the Wilson Bela LS, measured at 356 g, uses a glass and carbon blend and is more powerful than the classic but less than the Pro.

reviews.creator: Dani 13
reviews.summary: Tests the racket in defense, at the net, in the middle of the court and on smashes, comparing it with the previous version. Finds a medium hard feel with a 24K carbon face and Power Foam rubber, more ball output and more rebound than before. Rates the sweet spot as good, with some vibration when hitting off to the sides. Notes that the 372 g weight tires the arm over time, though the extra output means less gesture is needed. Finds control worse at fast pace, where balls easily end up in the glass. Calls smash power quite good and the racket easier than earlier Belas.
reviews.more: Compares the rebound to the Adidas Metalbone HRD, a little less exaggerated and with a little less smash power. Says the previous Bela Pro gave more calm at fast pace, while this one needs adapting to the bounce. Notes the balance is now lower, at 26 cm, which helps hide the weight. Advises dropping the tip and adding weight when accelerating at the net or mid court, as otherwise balls go to the glass. Ranks smash first, then defense, then viper and bandeja and volley about equal.
highlights: 24K carbon face and Power Foam rubber
more ball output and more rebound

reviews.creator: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi
reviews.summary: Tests the racket at a club in Rome and scores each shot out of 10. Finds much more maneuverability than the V 2.5, with an impact feel of about 6.7, between a Delta Pro and the V 2.5. Gives 9.5 for the volley, 10 for the vibora, 9 for basic shots, 10 for the low wall exit and 9.5 for power smashes. Calls the sweet spot large for such an attacking racket. Holds back top marks on power because other rackets give more. Rates value 5.5 out of 10. Recommends it for intermediate-advanced to pro players, from about 3 to 3.5 on Playtomic.
reviews.more: Places the impact feel in the same segment as the Metalbone 3.4 and the T10 18K aluminized, a little softer than the V 2.5, which was already softer than the V 2.0. Finds the block similar to the DeFi Pro. Says the racket has a teardrop shape, 24K carbon faces, a medium-hard Power Foam core and a double bridge that helps damp vibrations. Notes that the price was lowered for this launch. Advises beginners and lower intermediate players against it, since easier rackets exist.
highlights: much more maneuverability than the V 2.5
